Where they are not, an admission is made only under K4's posture: a structural, decidable check at the site plus a recorded residual obligation with a named backstop ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows), [§28.11](#sec-collection-element-ownership)).
4. **Signature-level re-establishment.** A callee's declared signature announces its result's source set — the **type-announced** classification: read off the declared, pre-substitution type, [K6.2](#sec-kernel-k6) being the frame instance — as a function of the call's receiver and arguments — the bare-type-parameter source set, the deferred-activation frame's carried sources — and every caller re-establishes the set against its own actuals. A borrow whose source no caller could re-establish (a scope-bound local, a temporary, a parameter source the signature does not announce) may not be returned.

<a id="sec-kernel-k3"></a>
**K3 — Discharge and consumption.** The obligation on an owned value is discharged at exactly one of the eleven **owned-consuming positions** — the rows of the consume table below, its single definition site, grouped by the three consume families. Three principles (K3.13–K3.15) follow the table.

<a id="sec-consume-table"></a>
**The consume table.** Reading rules, normative with the table. The **Position** column enumerates the consuming positions for *any* owned value; the **Spelling**, **Post-state**, and **Frozen** columns describe the case where the consumed operand is an owned **binding** — a local or an `owned` parameter — since a fresh producer or unbound temporary in the same position involves no binding, and no marker, post-state, or freeze question arises (K3.13). Kills of a **field or collection slot** are outside the Frozen column entirely ([K5.6](#sec-kernel-k5)). The Frozen column reads off [K5](#sec-kernel-k5)'s criterion; verdicts marked † are [K5.3](#sec-kernel-k5)'s and do **not** hold under the two recorded shapes that fail K5's conjunct (ii) — [§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters)'s storage-bounded captures ([K5.7](#sec-kernel-k5)) and [§30.12](#sec-thread-synchronization)'s guard interiors ([K5.8](#sec-kernel-k5)) — each stated at its home. The three rows tagged K4.2 are exactly the **site-announced kills**; this table is the definition site of that closed set and of each kill's disposal moment. A *conditional* kill of any row joins to **maybe-consumed** ([K7.4](#sec-kernel-k7)) — one clause, applying to every row.

| K | Position | Spelling | Post-state of the binding | Frozen? | Disposal moment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | **Family 1 — transfers into owned destinations** (K3.1–K3.4, K3.12) | | | | |
| K3.1 | store into an `owned` field or owning-collection slot, including through a `set(owned)` accessor ([§23.3](#sec-block-form-properties)) | none — the declared slot announces (marker-free) | **moved-from** — a later read is an error until reassigned | frozen (K5.1) | none here — the new holder's |
| K3.2 | `return` under an `owned` return type, or under an unmarked **mint-announcing** return type — `Task`-family in a non-`async` body, iterable-family in a non-iterator body ([§29.5](#sec-return-not-allowed-in-iterator-methods) bars plain `return` in iterator bodies) | none — the declared return type announces (marker-free) | **moved-from** | frozen (K5.1) | none here — the caller's |
| K3.3 | an `owned` argument ([§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers)) | `move x` at the call site | **moved-from** | frozen (K5.1) | none here — the callee's |
| K3.4 | a marked binding or assignment transfer — `var y := move x;`, `y := move x;`, `using var y := move x;` (the anonymous adoption `using var _ := move x;` included, [§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)) — the marked owning-match scrutinee `case move x of …` ([§35.5](#sec-owning-match)) — and the **marked arm transfer**: `move x` as an if-expression branch or an expression-`case` arm result ([§20](#sec-the-if-expression), [§19.2](#sec-arms)), consuming on the path where its arm is selected | `move x` | **moved-from** (an arm: on the selected path; joins per K7.4) | frozen (K5.1) | none here — the new holder's |
| K3.12 | for move-only values ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)), any store into an owning location | none ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)'s scope note: unmarked assignment and plain passing move) | **moved-from** | frozen (K5.1) | none here — the new holder's |
| — | **Family 2 — ownership-taking kills and transfers** (K3.5–K3.9) | | | | |
| K3.5 | the operand of a Pattern B `await` ([§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal)) | none — the keyword announces | **moved-from** | **unfrozen** (K4.2, K5.3)† | at the await, on all outgoing edges including fault and cancel ([§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal)) |
| K3.6 | the owned parameter-or-plain-local source of a Pattern A chaining `return await` ([§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal)) | `return await` — the form is the keyword | **moved-from** | **unfrozen** ([K5.4](#sec-kernel-k5): by the criterion — (i) at the form, (ii) by the intact-referent disjunct) | none at the site — deferred to the outer task's teardown, transitively (no flag the K4.1 backstop can schedule) |
| K3.7 | the operand of `yield return` in an owning iterator ([§29.2](#sec-iterator-yield-ownership)) | none — the declared owning interface announces | **moved-from** | frozen (K5.1; [§29.2](#sec-iterator-yield-ownership)) | none here — the consumer's |
| K3.8 | the operand of `throw` ([§31.1](#sec-the-throw-operand)) | none — the keyword announces | **moved-from** | **unfrozen** (K4.2, K5.3)† | after the matching catch arm completes, or at termination if uncaught ([§31.1](#sec-the-throw-operand)) |
| K3.9 | explicit disposal of an owned binding — the marker-free discard `_ := x;` ([§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)), or a `Dispose()` call (`x.Dispose()`, `x?.Dispose()`, `x!.Dispose()`) on an owned receiver, the receiver-classification rules, including the declaring-type field admission, being [§28.6](#sec-leak-prevention)'s | the discard statement itself, or the `Dispose()` call — no marker | **explicitly-disposed** — straight-line use afterward is [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)'s mandatory use-after-dispose warning | **unfrozen** (K4.2, K5.3)† | at the end of the discard statement ([§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)), or at the call |
| — | **Family 3 — displacement** (K3.11) | | | | |
| K3.11 | reassignment of an owned location — a consume of the **displaced** value (drop-on-overwrite, [§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields)) | the kill of the displaced value is unspelled; the RHS follows the state-match rule (*Ownership state of locals* below) | none arises — the kill's subject is the **displaced** value; the binding takes the new value and stays readable | frozen at a binding (K5.2); slot overwrites are outside the freeze (K5.6) | after the RHS is evaluated (RHS-first; [K9.5](#sec-kernel-k9) is the slot analog) |

   Three principles govern the enumeration:

13. **Marker economy.** A consume is spelled by the transfer marker (`move x`) except at a **marker-free position**, where the target or keyword already announces it — the table's Spelling column is the definition site of which is which. An **unmarked read of a class-typed binding never consumes**: `var b := a;` is always a borrow for class-typed `a`. (Move-only *value* types move on unmarked assignment and plain parameter passing, per [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)'s own scope note; K3.12.) Fresh producers need no marker anywhere (no live binding is invalidated).
14. **Affinity.** An owned value that reaches its scope's end undischarged and not moved-from is disposed there implicitly; the implicit drop of a plain-`var` local or undischarged `owned` parameter carries the must-use warning (a lint over a sound program; not at a trivial-dispose value — [K1.6](#sec-kernel-k1)'s ceremony exemption).
15. **Edge parity.** The exception edge performs the same implicit disposal as the normal edge, on the single establishment-ordered cleanup stack; the only difference is the lint. Unbound temporaries join the same stack at their production.

<a id="sec-kernel-k4"></a>
**K4 — Kills, site-announcement, and the backstop posture.** A **kill** ends a value's life under its current holder. Three independent bits classify every kill — each a property the kernel already reasons with, named here once:

- **obligation-moves** — does the obligation leave this holder for a new one? (If not, the value dies here.)
- **flag-set** — does the kill guarantee the per-instance disposed flag is set, on a schedule the K4.1 backstop can rely on?
- **keyword-visible** — is the kill spelled at the site by a keyword or a call the reader sees?

The [consume table](#sec-consume-table) records the verdicts these bits decide, and each bit is recoverable from it: **obligation-moves** from the Post-state column (*moved-from* exactly where the kill moves; *explicitly-disposed* where it does not and the flag is set); **flag-set** from the Disposal-moment column (the K4.2 rows and displacement set the flag at the stated moment; the family-1 transfer rows and the K3.6 deferral guarantee none the K4.1 backstop can schedule); **keyword-visible** from the Spelling column (a keyword, the marker, or the `Dispose()` call — not a bare declared-type announcement, and not reassignment). Displacement (row K3.11) is outside the post-state question by its subject: the kill there is of the **displaced** value — the binding itself takes the new value and stays readable. The freeze verdict is [K5](#sec-kernel-k5)'s criterion, read off in the table's Frozen column; a *conditional* kill of any row joins to **maybe-consumed** ([K7.4](#sec-kernel-k7)); kills of a **field or collection slot** are outside the freeze entirely ([K5.6](#sec-kernel-k5)).

   The posture, in three clauses:

1. **The backstop.** Disposal is idempotent and flag-setting; in checked disposal mode ([§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)) any later use through any alias faults deterministically as `DisposedAccessException`, and unchecked mode is the same language with the check elided. This is the runtime backstop every trust admission names.
2. **Site-announced kills.** A kill that is both **keyword-visible at the kill site** and **flag-backstopped** is **site-announced**, and is permitted while borrows of the value live: the announcement is the reader's notice and the flag is the safety net. The closed set is exactly the [consume table](#sec-consume-table)'s three rows tagged K4.2 — explicit disposal (`Dispose()` or the discard), `throw x`, and Pattern B `await` — with each kill's post-state and disposal moment in the table's columns.
3. **Recorded trust, or nothing.** Where an admission's temporal guarantee can neither be statically compared (K2.3) nor flag-backstopped — the domain clause ([§28.3](#sec-borrow-lifetime-rules)'s field-store bullet, clause 4): a borrowed-from object transferred to, or made reachable from, another domain stays alive, so no flag is ever set — the rule must either reject statically or carry an **individually recorded trust clause**. The recorded clauses (field-held, collection-held, and frame-held borrows versus domain transfer; [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows), [§30.1](#sec-async-methods)) are the model's honest limit, and no new admission may be made without recording its clause or its backstop. The recorded set is enumerable, and the trust-admission report mode ([§28.3](#sec-diagnostics)) enumerates it at every site.

<a id="sec-kernel-k5"></a>
**K5 — The freeze.** Consuming an owned **binding** (a local or `owned` parameter; the consume table's positions) while a live local borrow of its current value exists is a compile error, **unless the kill is unfrozen** — and a kill is unfrozen exactly when both hold (rationale [§5.1](Bezel_Design_Rationale.md#sec-owned-not-borrows)):

   **(i)** it is **keyword-visible at the kill site** (the reader's notice), and
   **(ii)** the disposed flag it guarantees is an **admissible backstop for every borrow that survives the kill** (the safety net): the kill flags the object those borrows are sourced from, and each surviving borrow's referent is left either flagged by the same kill or intact and disposal-tracked, so a later stale use still faults ([§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)). (ii) fails in exactly two recorded shapes, and in no other — the kill releases what the surviving borrows reference while flagging only their source ([§30.12](#sec-thread-synchronization)'s guard kills, clause 8), or the admission that produced those borrows forswore the backstop for a fully static bound ([§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters)'s storage-bounded capture, clause 7). Every other surviving borrow is backstopped by the kill's own flag — the interior-borrow dispensations that leave their referent intact included (`Shared<T>.Get()`, [§28.13](#sec-shared-ownership); the collection element and receiver-sourced reads, [§28.11](#sec-element-slot-policy), [§28.3](#sec-producers)).

   The criterion is stated here once; the [consume table](#sec-consume-table)'s Frozen column reads it off, and every placement — [§30.12](#sec-thread-synchronization)'s guard instance included, clause 8 — is its consequence, not a second list:

1. the family-1 transfers and owning-iterator `yield return` (the table's rows K3.1–K3.4, K3.7, K3.12) are frozen — each **fails (ii)**: an obligation-moving kill sets no flag, and its surviving borrows' referents are neither flagged nor guaranteed intact for the borrows' whole life;
2. drop-on-overwrite of a binding (row K3.11) is frozen although it disposes — it **fails (i)**: the reassignment is not keyword-visible as a kill of the *old* value, and the flag it does set is irrelevant once (i) fails;
3. the [K4.2](#sec-kernel-k4) site-announced kills (rows K3.5, K3.8, K3.9) are unfrozen — each **satisfies (i)**, and **satisfies (ii)** wherever the surviving borrows are backstopped by the kill's own flag, which is every case but the two recorded in clauses 7 and 8;
4. a Pattern A chaining `return await x` (row K3.6) is unfrozen **by the criterion**: (i) holds — the `return await` keywords are the kill site ([§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal)) — and (ii) holds because every borrow that survives the kill has its referent left **intact and disposal-tracked**: the new holder (the outer task) cannot dispose the chained task before the body, `finally` blocks included, completes, so no surviving borrow needs a flag;
5. the freeze is **body-local by construction** — the clause bounds what *liveness* means, not what is frozen: liveness is the backward dataflow over one body, borrows are traced through `using var` pins, live closures, and locals of borrow-bearing record or inline-array type or of choice types that hold borrows ([§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal); [§15.1.2](#sec-inline-array-members); [§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)'s holds-borrows property), and this is why a closure may not consume its captured owned bindings (K2 + decidability);
6. **fields and collection slots are not frozen** — the clause bounds what the freeze's *subject* is: slot aliases are not body-local, and a slot kill disposes — the K4 backstop is real there; the slot kill *by move* is instead governed by K4.3's domain clause ([§28.3](#sec-consume-site-freeze), [§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields), [§28.11](#sec-collection-element-ownership));
7. a [§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters) storage admission freezes the admitted captures against the site-announced kills as well — a **derivation from (ii)**, not an exception: the surviving borrow lives in a stored callback whose invocation site is statically invisible at the kill, and the storage admission's promise is a fully static bound, so a runtime flag is not an admissible backstop for it — stated with its reason at [§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters), under axiom [A11](#sec-axiom-register)'s forms;
8. a [§30.12](#sec-thread-synchronization) guard's site-announced kills are frozen while borrows sourced from the guard live — likewise a **derivation from (ii)**: killing a guard sets the disposed flag on the *guard*, while the surviving borrows reference the lock's *interior*, on which no flag is set, the lock released out from under them — stated with its reason at [§30.12](#sec-thread-synchronization).
<a id="sec-kernel-k6"></a>
**K6 — Frames are values.** A deferred activation — a task (`Task`, `Task<T>`, `OwningTask<T>`), an iterator or async-iterator frame (enumerable or enumerator, borrowing or owning), a lazy query — is a **value** with an ordinary K1 classification that additionally **carries a source set** (K2): the constructing call's receiver, its plain reference-typed arguments, and the capture-set contributions of its plain function-typed arguments, transitively.

1. **The bound.** Carried sources must outlive the frame's bound: **settlement** for a task ([§30.1](#sec-async-methods)); **completion or disposal** for an iterator frame ([§29.4](#sec-lazy-evaluation), [§29.7](#sec-disposal-of-partially-consumed-iterators)); the **single consumption point** for a lazy query, which is thereby affine ([§29.11](#sec-multiple-enumeration)).
2. **Announcement by declared type.** Frame-carrying classification is **type-announced** — keyed on the callee's declared, pre-substitution return type: a `Task`-family type, a [§29.3](#sec-iterator-methods)/[§30.7](#sec-asynchronous-programming-async-iterators) iterable or enumerator interface, a lazy query — and every caller re-establishes the carried set against its own actuals (K2.4). This is what admits returning a composed frame, and what rejects a returned frame carrying a scope-bound local, `using var`, or temporary.
3. **Containers: calls mint, storage lends.** A call whose declared return type is **mint-announcing** — a `Task`-family type, or an iterable-family type (a [§29.3](#sec-iterator-methods)/[§30.7](#sec-asynchronous-programming-async-iterators) iterable or enumerator interface, or a lazy query) — produces a fresh **owned** frame at every call site; a read of frame **storage** (property, field, slot) lends a borrow of the storage; callee-side, the unmarked mint-announcing return type transfers the container like an `owned` return (axiom [A15](#sec-axiom-register)'s self-returning enumerator excepted).
4. **Frames versus the freeze.** Frame-held borrows live in the frame, not in any local borrow binding, so K5 cannot see them; their outlives-obligation is the K4.3-recorded settlement clause ([§30.1](#sec-async-methods)), discharged trivially by awaiting before any source's scope exits and structurally by `TaskScope`. The abandonment idioms carry the residual explicitly.
5. **Interaction with K8.** A frame sourced by an unbound temporary must itself be consumed to its bound within the same full expression; a frame that escapes the expression is rejected — the reject-not-extend posture.

<a id="sec-kernel-k7"></a>
**K7 — The join rule.** At every control-flow join — statement merges, `??`, `if` expressions, expression-position `case` arms, loop back edges — a variable's or expression's state is the lattice meet, owned ⊑ borrowed:

1. owned ⊓ owned = **owned**, obligation carried forward (for expression arms: exactly one arm's value exists at runtime, so exactly one obligation);
2. borrowed ⊓ borrowed = **borrowed**, carrying the union of the arms' source sets (K2.2);
3. owned ⊓ borrowed = **rejected** — no single state is correct, and demoting owned would silently drop an obligation; the program equalizes the arms first;
4. owned ⊓ moved-from and owned ⊓ explicitly-disposed = **maybe-consumed** — unreadable after the join, no flow around a back edge into a use; scope-end disposal per-path;
5. `null`-literal and bottom-typed (`throw`) arms absorb to the other arm's state.

The direction is deliberate: rejection at 3 rather than demotion is what makes the meet leak-free (rationale [§5.6](Bezel_Design_Rationale.md#sec-the-lattice-direction-at-control-flow-joins)).

<a id="sec-kernel-k8"></a>
**K8 — The full-expression boundary.** A **full expression** is a maximal expression — not a subexpression of any larger expression — at the enumerated positions (initializers, assignment RHSs, expression statements, each *evaluation* of a condition or guard, `for` sources, `return`/`throw`/`yield return` operands, `case` scrutinees).

1. Unbound owned temporaries are disposed at their full expression's end, after their uses; on the exception edge, during unwinding in reverse production order.
2. Conditions and guards are per-evaluation boundaries: temporaries never accumulate across iterations.
3. A `case` scrutinee's boundary is the whole construct — pattern bindings are borrows of the scrutinee, and the temporary survives arm selection, guard evaluation, and the selected arm's completion — in statement position exactly as in expression position.
4. A temporary is an admissible borrow source only within its boundary; a borrow or frame that would escape it is **rejected, never lifetime-extended** — the language has no general lifetime-extension mechanism ([§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal); rationale [§5.24](Bezel_Design_Rationale.md#sec-the-full-expression-boundary)). The escapes rejected are every escape [K2.3](#sec-kernel-k2) can compare — among them a binding, store, capture, `return` or `yield return` of the borrow in the producing body — and every retention a declaration announces — among them a returned frame (K6.5), a frame carrying the borrow taken by an `owned` parameter or owning slot (`Task.FireAndForget`, [§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)), a borrow-bearing record's field or a holds-borrows choice's payload ([§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal), [§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)), a `scoped` parameter ([§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters)), and a `ref` or `out` location. A plain parameter announces none: a callee that stores it holds the borrow under the borrowed-field rule's or the borrowing-collection store rule's recorded residual ([§28.3](#sec-borrow-lifetime-rules), [§28.11](#sec-borrowing-collections)), and the temporary is still disposed at its boundary (K8.1).
5. A binding atom ([§17.15](#sec-the-binding-atom)) is the boundary for its own bindings: a binding whose initializer is an owned production is a **named unbound owned temporary** whose boundary is the atom — disposed at the atom's completion if undischarged, after the body's evaluation, in reverse clause order; clause 4 applies to the atom boundary verbatim.

<a id="sec-kernel-k9"></a>
**K9 — Fields are object state, not scope state.** A field's obligation belongs to the object: it is discharged by the destructor cascade (owned fields, reverse declaration order) or by drop-on-overwrite, never by any scope's end, and no scope-end machinery ever touches it. Consequences:

1. every plain read of an owned field lends (K1.5); the only owned read is `move x.f` — and `move coll[i]` for owning slots — which puts the slot in moved-from state ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression));
2. **the restoration rule**: every control-flow path from a `move` of a field or slot to the enclosing method's exit — normal, `throw`, `yield break`, and every exception edge raised by an intervening throwable expression — must reassign the slot: the object must never escape the method with a hole a destructor could observe ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression));
3. a destructor body is exempt from restoration (teardown: no future read exists), and a constructor's `move` is governed by definite assignment before first assignment ([§7.9](#sec-definite-assignment-for-non-nullable-fields));
4. static owned fields admit no `move`: the restoration obligation is scoped to a single method, and static state is observable across method boundaries, so no per-method window can cover it ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression), [§22.12](#sec-static-members));
5. drop-on-overwrite (K3.11) is RHS-first, so a throwing RHS leaves the slot untouched and still-owned — restoration idioms (`_resource := fresh;` onto a moved-from slot) are non-throwable ([§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields)).

The build-before-take discipline and the throwable-expression classification are derivations under K9, stated in [§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression); the per-slot conservative tracking for non-constant indices is stated in [§28.11](#sec-move-on-a-collection-slot).

<a id="sec-axiom-register"></a>
#### The axiom register (A1–A15)

Eleven axioms (and four tombstones). Each is a rule the kernel cannot derive — a recorded design decision — and each is the extension point a future ruling in its area must name; a tombstone row records a retired axiom and points at the retiring revision's changelog entry. Ordering is by home section; one-line reasons here, full recorded reasons in rationale [§5.26](Bezel_Design_Rationale.md#sec-the-ownership-kernel). Axiom ids are stable: new axioms append; a deleted axiom leaves a tombstone row pointing at the deleting revision's changelog entry.

| # | Axiom | Home | Recorded reason (one line) |

<a id="sec-ownership-state-of-locals"></a>
#### Ownership state of locals

A local's ownership state is one of [K1](#sec-kernel-k1)'s classifications, inferred from the form that introduces the local (the state names and their meanings — including the auxiliary **uninitialized**, **polymorphic-null**, and **explicitly-disposed** states — are K1's):

- `using var x := expr;` where `expr` is an owned producer or a marked transfer (`using var x := move y;`) is **owned**, additionally subject to scope-based disposal at the end of the enclosing block. When `expr` is a borrow — for example a call without an owned return, a field or indexer read, or an unmarked read of a **borrow-state** named binding — `x` is instead a **borrow-pin** with no disposal obligation ([§28.10](#sec-using-var)); an unmarked read of a **class- or interface-typed** named **owned** binding is rejected there ([§28.10](#sec-using-var)), and an unmarked read of a **move-only value** binding moves instead ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)).
- `var x := expr;` takes the ownership state of `expr` (see *Producers* below); plain `var` does not change the state. A read of a *named owned binding* on the right-hand side is a **borrow** unless it carries the explicit transfer marker — `var y := move x;` ([§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers); see *Move semantics for owned locals* below).
- `var x: T;` without an initializer at a **non-defaultable** `T` is **uninitialized**: it holds no value, carries no obligation and no borrow source, and may not be read until assigned ([§7.9](#sec-definite-assignment-for-non-nullable-fields)); at a **defaultable** `T` the declaration is the initialization ([§7.9](#sec-definite-assignment-for-non-nullable-fields)'s *Default initialization*) and the binding carries no obligation and no borrow source either. The declaration fixes **no** ownership state (the adoption clause below).

**State match on reassignment** (derives: [K1.7](#sec-kernel-k1) + [K3.11](#sec-kernel-k3)). Reassignment to an existing `var x` is state-matched: an **owned-state** LHS requires an owned RHS — a fresh producer, or a named owned binding under the explicit transfer marker (`x := move y;`) — and disposes the displaced value per drop-on-overwrite ([§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields)), subject to the consume-site freeze below; a **borrowed-state** LHS requires a borrow (or `null`) RHS. Assigning a borrow to an owned-state LHS, or an owned value to a borrowed-state LHS, is rejected — the mismatch would silently drop or double-hold a disposal obligation.

**Adoption** (derives: [K1.7](#sec-kernel-k1) + [K3.11](#sec-kernel-k3), vacuously — nothing is displaced). A LHS holding **no classified value** is not state-matched: there is no displaced obligation to drop and none to double-hold, so an RHS of either classification is admissible and the local **adopts** that classification. Two states qualify, and no others: an **uninitialized** local (`var x: T;` at a non-defaultable `T`, the bullet above), and one in the **polymorphic null state** (`var x: T? := null;` — the null-literal producers row — or that same declaration with no initializer, [§7.9](#sec-definite-assignment-for-non-nullable-fields)'s *Default initialization* supplying the `null`). The adopted state is that of the first assignment that reaches the local **on each path** — owned from a fresh producer *or a marked transfer*, borrowed from an unmarked binding read or any other borrow; for a polymorphic-null LHS, of the first **non-null** such assignment, a `null` RHS having no value to own and deciding nothing. From that assignment onward the local is state-matched by the rule above; where two paths adopt different states, [K7](#sec-kernel-k7)'s meet governs the merge (below). This is what the two worked patterns below turn on: the same declaration `var x: Stream;` leaves `x` **borrowed** in Pattern 1 and **owned** in Pattern 2 — the assignments decide, not the declaration.

At every control-flow join the compiler applies [K7](#sec-kernel-k7)'s meet to each variable's tracked state (K7.1–K7.4). Two consequences are worth naming: merging a parameter-sourced borrow with a receiver-sourced borrow is fine — K7.2 carries the union, and rejection arises only at a later use or escape that violates a carried constraint; and after a K7.4 join to **maybe-consumed** the variable may not be read, borrowed from, or consumed, and may not flow around a loop back edge into any use, while scope-end auto-drop applies per-path (the same per-slot tracking [§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression) uses). A join at which one edge leaves the local **uninitialized** is not a meet of two classifications and does not reach K7's lattice at all: after such a join the local is **not definitely assigned** and may not be read ([§7.9](#sec-definite-assignment-for-non-nullable-fields)), while the classification each assigning edge adopted is carried **per-path** — an owned value live at scope end on an assigning path is disposed there by [K3.14](#sec-kernel-k3)'s auto-drop, exactly as on any other path, using the same per-path machinery [K7.4](#sec-kernel-k7) names. The analysis is keyed on the definite-assignment machinery of [§7.9](#sec-definite-assignment-for-non-nullable-fields); diagnostics should point at the offending use, not the declaration.

To compile a mixed merge, **the program** must equalize the branches before the merge; the compiler never equalizes for it (K7.3 rejects). The two standard patterns, as worked examples — both resting on the adoption clause above, and equalizing in opposite directions:

```bezel
// Pattern 1: equalize to borrowed — both branches bind x to a source
// that outlives the merge.
var x: Stream;                       // x will be a borrow at the merge
if condition then
  using var scratch := new FileStream(path, FileMode.Create);  // owned: used and discharged in-branch
  primary.Reset(scratch);            // scratch's work is done here
  x := primary.Stream;               // x borrows primary (outlives the if)
else
  x := otherSource.Stream;           // x borrows otherSource (outlives the if)
end;
// At the merge, x is borrowed on both branches, and both sources
// (primary, otherSource) outlive the merge point. The using var
// scratch was discharged at its own scope end; x never borrowed it.

// Pattern 2: produce an owned value on both branches.
var x: Stream;
if condition then
  x := new FileStream(path, FileMode.Create);
else
  x := otherSource.CloneStream();   // returns owned Stream
end;
// At the merge, x is owned on both branches.
// x reaches an owned slot, is disposed, or auto-drops at scope end (§28.3).
```

Where one branch is a **named owned binding**, the marked arm transfer ([K3.4](#sec-kernel-k3)) writes the same equalization as one expression: `var x := (if useFresh then new FileStream(path, FileMode.Create) else move cached);` — both arms owned, `cached` consumed only on the selected path and per-path consumed after the construct ([K7.4](#sec-kernel-k7)).

Equalizing to borrowed (Pattern 1) does not merely require both branches to *be* borrows — it requires each branch's borrow source to outlive the merge point ([K2.1](#sec-kernel-k2)). Binding `x` in one branch to a borrow of a `using var` discharged at that branch's end does **not** equalize the merge: the borrow's source is already gone by the time `x` is read after the `if`, and the borrow-lifetime rule rejects it. The `using var` completes its work *within* the branch; `x` takes its post-merge value from a source that lives past the `if` (as `primary` and `otherSource` do above).

<a id="sec-producers"></a>
#### Producers

The ownership state of an expression is determined by the expression form — the worked enumeration under [K1.5](#sec-kernel-k1); rule-carrying rows carry their derivation tags:

| Expression | Ownership |
|---|---|
| `null` literal; `default(T?)` and any other `default` form producing `null` ([§17.11](#sec-the-default-operator) — the bridge is §17.11's value rule, deliberately not [§17.14](#sec-constant-expressions) constancy, which `default` does not have) | Context-typed; this row covers the literal and a null-producing `default` expression identically. `null` has no value to own, so it is **compatible with either an owned target or a borrowed target**: assigned to an owned location it leaves that location owned-currently-null (disposal of null is a no-op); assigned to a borrowed location it is the borrowed-currently-null value with no source. A local declared `var x: T? := null;` — or initialized from a null-producing `default` form — is in the **polymorphic null state** ([K1](#sec-kernel-k1)): its ownership state is decided by the first non-null assignment, per the adoption clause of *Ownership state of locals*. A local that remains at null for its entire lifetime is statically dead-storable; the compiler may emit a warning but the program is well-formed. |
| `new T(...)` | Owned |
| `typeof(T)` ([§17.10](#sec-the-typeof-operator)), and any call whose declared return type is `Type` — `value.GetType()` ([§8.2](#sec-gettype)) included | Not applicable — `Type` is runtime-managed ([§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types)): the expression carries no ownership classification, lends no borrow, and constrains no lifetime. A `Type`-returning member is the [announcement table](#sec-announcement-table)'s **row 7** at every callee kind, so a **static** method may declare it and no `owned Type` spelling exists. |
| Collection literal (`[1, 2, 3]`) targeting a reference type (`Array<T>`, `OwningArray<T>`, `Set<T>`, `Dictionary<K, V>`, etc.) | Owned |
| Collection literal (`[1, 2, 3]`) targeting an inline-array type (`[N]T`, including `[N owned]T?`) | Not applicable — produces a value. For move-only `[N owned]…` targets, the value is move-only ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)). |
| Any **call** — instance, static, or extension method, or a function-value invocation | Classified by the [announcement table](#sec-announcement-table) below: the callee's declared, pre-substitution return kind × callee kind decides. `owned T` → **Owned** (row 1). A **mint-announcing** type → **Owned frame** (rows 2–3 — calls mint). A plain concrete class or interface type → **Borrowed** (row 4: instance — source the receiver; extension — the receiver parameter, [§26.7](#sec-ownership-in-extensions); static — rejected at the declaration; function value — see the row's cell). A **bare type parameter** → the source-set classification of rows 5–6 (*Bare-type-parameter returns* below). A value, `string`, or runtime-managed result → not applicable (row 7, [§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types)). A **move-only value type** → **Owned** move-only value (row 8, [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)). Property, field, indexer, local, and slot **reads** are never classified by that table — the storage rows of this table govern them. |
| Field access `obj.f` where `f` is `owned` | Borrowed (source: `obj`) |
| `move obj.f` where `f` is `owned` | Owned. Field is left in moved-from state and must be reassigned before the surrounding method exits ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression)). |
| Field access `obj.f` where `f` is not `owned` | Borrowed (source: `obj`) |
| Indexer access `coll[i]` | Borrowed (qualified by family, reconciling [§28.11](#sec-element-slot-policy)). Owning-family collection: source is `coll`, and the borrow is additionally valid only until the slot is mutated (an indexer-set, `Remove*`, or `Clear` disposes the referent — a mid-scope value kill whose dominating straight-line subset draws [§28.11](#sec-owning-collections)'s element-borrow use-after-removal warning and which is otherwise not statically tracked per slot; checked-mode backstop, [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal), stdlib §4.5). Borrowing-family collection: the true source is the element's original owner ([§28.11](#sec-element-slot-policy) — the collection is a transit point); the compiler cannot identify that owner structurally and enforces the collection binding as the proxy bound, the owner-outlives-use residual being the same trust regime as field-held borrows. |
| Range slice `arr[r]` on `Array<T>` ([§15.6](#sec-slicing)) | Owned — a fresh `Array<T>`, the compiler-recognized `Slice(r: Range<int>): owned Array<T>` form (stdlib §4.4); **not** the indexer row above. The container is owned by the caller and discharged under the standard rules; class-typed elements are borrows copied as borrows, their sources unchanged. |
| Property access `obj.P` (instance getter) | Borrowed (source: `obj`). Getters are borrow-producing positions — a getter may not return a fresh owned value ([§28.6](#sec-leak-prevention)). |
| Static property access `T.P` (class-typed result) | Borrowed (source: the declaring type's static storage — [K2](#sec-kernel-k2)'s always-live source: process-lived, so every intra-program liveness constraint is satisfied; static state is disposed only at program exit, [§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order)). |
| Static field access `T.f` — or the bare in-scope spelling `f` of the declaring type's own static field — with class- or interface-typed result | Borrowed (source: the declaring type's static storage — [K2](#sec-kernel-k2)'s always-live source, exactly as the `T.P` row above). The field's form — `owned`, `readonly` without `owned` ([§22.13](#sec-static-class-typed-fields-without-owned)), or an admitted mutable static ([§22.12](#sec-static-members) rule 2) — does not change the classification: every admissible form keeps its referents alive to process exit ([§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order); §22.12 rule 2's overwrite-never-disposes store semantics). |
| `move coll[i]` on an owning collection | Owned. The slot is left in moved-from state and must be reassigned before the surrounding method exits ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression)). Which collection types admit the form — and the per-family exclusions — is stated once, at [§28.11](#sec-move-on-a-collection-slot). |
| Local-variable read `x` where `x` is owned (a class-typed owned local, or a local of move-only value type per [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)) | Classified by the position the read appears in (see *Consuming positions for an owned-local read*, following this table). In an **owned-consuming position**, the read transfers ownership out of `x` and `x` takes the [consume table](#sec-consume-table)'s post-state (see *Move semantics*). In a **borrowing position**, `x` retains ownership and the value is borrowed for the consuming operation. |
| Local-variable read `x` where `x` is borrowed | Borrowed (source: same as `x`'s source) |
| Parameter `p` declared `owned p: T` | Owned |
| Parameter `p` (no modifier) | Borrowed (source: caller) |
| `this` | Borrowed (source: caller) — for a copyable value-kind receiver, the call's fixed receiver value, a full-expression temporary bounded by the call ([§9.4](#sec-value-receivers-are-borrows); [K8.4](#sec-kernel-k8)); for a move-only receiver, the receiver's storage, borrowed in place and bounded by the call ([§9.4](#sec-value-receivers-are-borrows) *Move-only receivers*) |
| `x as T` | Borrowed (source: same as `x`'s source if `x` is borrowed; `x` itself if `x` is owned). The cast does not move from `x`; `x` retains its ownership state. The result is nullable. See [§17.4](#sec-the-is-is-not-and-as-operators) for the rationale. |
| `x!` ([§17.8](#sec-the-null-forgiving-operator)) | `x`'s own classification. Over a named owned binding it is the read of `x`, classified by its position as the owned-local-read row above classifies `x`; a borrow keeps `x`'s source; a fresh producer's `!` is owned. |
| `a ?? b` (null-coalescing, [§7.7](#sec-null-coalescing-and-=)) | The **meet** of the ownership states of `a` and `b` per [K7](#sec-kernel-k7) — the same two-branch merge as the control-flow join above (K7.1–K7.3: owned ⊓ owned = **owned**, exactly one arm's value produced and discharged; borrowed ⊓ borrowed = **borrowed** with the union of sources; mixed = **rejected** — equalize the arms first). A **named owned binding** written as an arm is an *unmarked read* and therefore a **borrow** arm (K3.13; the transfer marker is rejected in `??`-operand position — axiom [A7](#sec-axiom-register)): `a ?? b` over two named owned locals consumes neither binding. To coalesce two named owned bindings into one owned result, use the marked arm transfer — `var r := (if a <> null then move a else move b);` ([K3.4](#sec-kernel-k3)) — or equalize by statement. A `null`-literal or bottom-typed (`throw`) arm absorbs to the other arm's state (K7.5), legitimizing the `x ?? throw …` shape ([§17.12](#sec-the-throw-expression)). The compound form `a ??= b` assigns into `a` and follows the same meet rule for the assigned-into location. |
| `(if c then v1 else v2)` ([§20](#sec-the-if-expression)); the result of an expression-position `case` ([§19.1](#sec-forms), [§19.2](#sec-arms)) | The **meet** of the arms' ownership states, identically to the `a ?? b` row above ([K7](#sec-kernel-k7) at expression joins; for `case` the meet ranges over every arm's result expression) — with one difference: the **marked arm** `move x` *is* admitted here (axiom A7 rejects it only in `??`-operand position), an **owned** producer and [K3.4](#sec-kernel-k3) transfer consuming on the path where its arm is selected, the binding joining per [K7.4](#sec-kernel-k7) after the construct. An **unmarked** read of a named owned binding remains a **borrow** arm (K3.13 — no silent consume); `throw` and `null`-literal arms absorb (K7.5; [§17.12](#sec-the-throw-expression)). |
| The binding atom `(var x := E; body)` ([§17.15](#sec-the-binding-atom)) | The **body's** classification, transparently — the atom is not a join (clauses and body evaluate unconditionally; no meet arises). Each clause is a *binding form*: its binding classifies per this table applied to its initializer — a borrow initializer yields a borrow binding carrying the initializer's sources; `var y := move x;` is [K3.4](#sec-kernel-k3)'s marked binding transfer; an owned production yields a **named unbound owned temporary bounded by the atom** ([K8.5](#sec-kernel-k8)), disposed at the atom's completion if undischarged. A borrow sourced by an atom binding may not escape the atom ([K8.4](#sec-kernel-k8) at the atom boundary) — in particular, a body whose value borrows an owned binding of the atom is rejected. The body is not a [K3.4](#sec-kernel-k3) marked-transfer position (no `move x` body in this revision). |
| Captured borrow inside a closure | Borrowed (source: same as the captured local's source). The closure value itself is runtime-managed; the captured borrow's lifetime is tracked separately. |
| Captured owned local inside a closure | Borrowed (source: the local's enclosing scope). Capturing does not transfer ownership; the closure cannot outlive the local's scope. See [§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types). |

**Consuming positions for an owned-local read.** The owned local-variable-read row above classifies the read by the position it appears in. The **owned-consuming positions** — the read consumes `x`, leaving it in the post-state the [consume table](#sec-consume-table)'s column records (moved-from, explicitly-disposed, or — at reassignment — the displaced value consumed) — are the table's eleven rows; which carry the explicit transfer marker and which are **marker-free** is the table's Spelling column ([K3.13](#sec-kernel-k3); *Move semantics for owned locals* below).

The **borrowing positions** — `x` retains ownership, and the value is borrowed for the consuming operation — are:

- a non-`owned` argument;
- an indexer or property access;
- an operand of a null-coalescing expression (`a ?? b` — the table's `??` row then sees a borrow arm; the marker is rejected in that position, axiom [A7](#sec-axiom-register)), or an **unmarked** if-expression branch or expression-`case` arm result (the arm-meet row sees a borrow arm; the *marked* form `move x` in those positions is instead the K3.4 arm transfer);
- the operand of a `yield return` in a borrowing iterator (a re-borrow, source the binding itself — [§29.2](#sec-iterator-yield-ownership));
- an **unmarked** local binding or assignment RHS over a **class- or interface-typed** binding — `var y := x;`, `y := x;`: a plain alias binding is a borrow of `x`, source `x` itself (at a move-only `x` the same spellings **move**, [K3.12](#sec-kernel-k3), [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types), [§28.10](#sec-using-var)); at a `using var` the same unmarked read is the borrow-pin over a borrow-state `x` and is rejected over an owned `x` ([§28.10](#sec-using-var));
- for move-only locals, a borrow of the value through indexing or equality comparison.
<a id="sec-announcement-table"></a>
#### The announcement table

One question decides the caller-side ownership of every call: *what does the callee's declared return type announce, and at which callee kind?* The table below is that rule's matrix — declared return kind × callee kind (derives: [K2.4](#sec-kernel-k2) + [K6.2](#sec-kernel-k6)/[K6.3](#sec-kernel-k6) — the type-announced doctrine, stated cell by cell). The paragraphs following this table carry each rule's reasoning and its callee-side admission in full, and the *Cite* column names them. Three reading rules govern every cell:

> **Keying.** Every row is read from the callee's **declared** return type, **before** generic substitution, with nullability stripped (`Task?`, `IEnumerable<T>?`, `T?` qualify as their unstripped kinds). No type-keyed row applies to a call whose declared return type an earlier row claims — in particular, a bare type parameter is never re-keyed by what a substitution makes it. A bare type parameter whose constraints exclude class and interface substitutions (`where T: value`) is the one exception to that precedence: it is **row 7's**, at every marker spelling — such a declaration is outside the classification rules on both sides (*Bare-type-parameter returns*; *Factory methods and sourceless returns* below), and `owned` on it is rejected at the declaration ([§28.1](#sec-where-the-owned-modifier-can-appear)).
>
> **Inheritance.** A member implementing or overriding a declaration classifies at **the declaration it implements**, at every call site, direct or dispatched; a bare-type-parameter row's potential source set is read from the **generic** declaration's signature, its source parameters identified positionally through the substitution. Interface dispatch is therefore not a column: it is the declaring signature's row.
>
> **Not calls.** Property, field, indexer, local, and slot **reads** are governed by the *Producers* table's storage rows, never by this table: a read of storage of a mint-announcing type lends a borrow of the storage — and a property *reference* over a mint-announcing-typed property is rejected at formation ([§27.6](#sec-method-references)), so the lend face never inhabits a minting slot.

| # | Declared return kind | Instance callee | Static callee | Extension callee | Function-value invocation | Callee-side admission | Cite |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **`owned T`** over a non-mint-announcing type (a concrete class or interface, or a bare type parameter — the marker claims the row) | **Owned** | **Owned** — an admissible static signature | **Owned** | **Owned** | Every return path supplies a fresh or owned value (`null` admissible under a nullable declared type — [K1](#sec-kernel-k1)'s null clause: a null operand owns nothing); a borrow is rejected. At value and runtime-managed substitutions of a bare-type-parameter `owned` return the marker is **erased** by the substitution ([§28.1](#sec-where-the-owned-modifier-can-appear)) and the result is a plain value. | [§28.8](#sec-ownership-transfer); *Producers*; [§28.6](#sec-leak-prevention) |
| 2 | **mint-announcing, unmarked** — a `Task`-family type (`Task`, `Task<T>`, `OwningTask<T>`) or an iterable-family type: one of the eight [§29.3](#sec-iterator-methods)/[§30.7](#sec-asynchronous-programming-async-iterators) iterable/enumerator interface heads, or a **lazy query** (compiler-known; a derived-interface-typed lazy operator mints by its kind, while `IOrderedEnumerable<T>`/`IGrouping<TKey, T>` stay outside the head set at every declared-type-keyed boundary) | **Owned frame** — calls mint | **Owned frame** | **Owned frame** | **Owned frame** | Every return path of a non-`async`, non-iterator body supplies a fresh or owned frame (`null` admissible under a nullable declared type; an `async` or iterator body satisfies this by construction); returning a **borrow** is rejected — a stored frame is re-exposed through a property, field, or collection slot, or at the concrete collection type. One named admission: the self-returning enumerator's `return this;`, axiom [A15](#sec-axiom-register), caller-side classification unchanged at every column. The full admission — sources, the call-bounded exclusion — is *Calls mint*, clauses 5–6. | *Calls mint for the mint-announcing families*; *Returning a deferred-activation frame* (the carried sources); [K6.3](#sec-kernel-k6) |
| 3 | **mint-announcing, explicitly `owned`** | identical to row 2 | identical to row 2 | identical to row 2 | identical to row 2 | identical to row 2 — the marker states the same contract with emphasis (`GetEnumerator(): owned IEnumerator<T>`, [§29.1](#sec-iterator-protocol); `Domain.Spawn(...): owned Task`, stdlib §6.8) | *Calls mint for the mint-announcing families* |
| 4 | **plain concrete class or interface type** (unmarked; claimed by no other row) — a trivial-dispose class such as `Array<T>` included (a class type, [§3.1](#sec-type-kinds)): it carries the free obligation ([K1.6](#sec-kernel-k1)), so its static return names no responsible party either | **Borrow**, source = the receiver | **rejected at the declaration** — nothing names a responsible party | **Borrow**, source = the receiver parameter ([§26.7](#sec-ownership-in-extensions)) | **Borrow**, carrying the **union of the function value itself and the sources every plain (non-`owned`) argument contributes** ([§28.3](#sec-argument-contributions)) — the function value contributes its captured borrows' sources transitively (the capture-set contribution, [§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)); the plain arguments cover the adapter-formed references that route a receiver through a parameter ([§27.6](#sec-method-references)'s instance property reference) and parameter-sourced lambda returns (a lambda may return the result of invoking its own function-typed parameter, the closure bullet, [§28.3](#sec-borrow-lifetime-rules), or a borrow reached through a borrow-bearing or holds-borrows parameter of its own). The result is never owned. | *Instance/extension:* return only a receiver-(parameter-)sourced borrow; a fresh owned value is rejected ([§28.6](#sec-leak-prevention)) — declare `owned`. *Static:* no admissible body — the signature is rejected; a **static-storage-sourced** borrow passes only through a **static property getter**, never a static method. *Lambda into such a slot:* `null` (nullable slot), a capture-sourced borrow, a plain-parameter-sourced borrow, or static storage; a fresh owned value rejected. | *Producers*; *Factory methods and sourceless returns*; *Borrow lifetime rules*; *Concrete-slot function bodies* |
| 5 | **bare type parameter `T`, non-empty potential source set** — the receiver (for an extension callee the receiver parameter; for a function-value invocation the function value), together with every plain parameter whose declared type mentions `T` | at class/interface substitutions a **Borrow** carrying the union of the contributing sources' liveness; at value/runtime-managed substitutions no borrow: a borrow-bearing record or inline array, or a choice that holds borrows, carries that union as its carried borrows, and any other value carries no constraint (*Bare-type-parameter returns*, caller-side clause 3; at a function-type substitution the result is a function value carrying the empty set: a function value reaches a position typed at the substituted parameter only through a set-erasing position, or a holder, a `return` or a `yield return` that admits only capture-free ones, *Borrow lifetime rules*' closure bullet) | as instance — an admissible static signature | as instance | as instance, the result carrying the function value's and every plain argument's contributions, whatever the argument's slot type, as in row 4 (*Bare-type-parameter returns*, caller-side clause 1) | Every return path supplies `null` or a borrow whose sources outlive the call — the receiver, a plain source parameter, or static storage; a fresh owned value, or a borrow of an owned local, a `using var`, an `owned` parameter, or a temporary, is rejected. Enforced **per instantiation category** ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2); inherited by implementations and overrides. **`Task`-family exclusion:** a member is inadmissible at an instantiation substituting a `Task`-family type for a parameter appearing as the **return slot of a function type** anywhere within a parameter's declared type; the iterable family carries no per-substitution exclusion — its laundering inhabitants are rejected inhabitant-side. **Function-type exclusion:** a member is inadmissible at an instantiation substituting a function type for a type parameter appearing within a parameter slot of a function type that occupies a parameter slot of a parameter's declared type. Full admission and exclusions: *Bare-type-parameter returns*. | *Bare-type-parameter returns*; [K2.4](#sec-kernel-k2) |
| 6 | **bare type parameter `T`, empty potential source set** | **cannot arise** — an instance callee always has a receiver | **rejected at the declaration** — spell `owned T` (admissible over every constraint domain under [§28.1](#sec-where-the-owned-modifier-can-appear)'s per-instantiation erasure) | **cannot arise** — the receiver parameter is a source | **cannot arise** — the function value is a source | the signature is rejected at the declaration (fresh production would make the caller-side result owned; a static-storage-sourced borrow would acquire a second owner), so no body arises | *Bare-type-parameter returns*; *Factory methods and sourceless returns* |
| 7 | **value type, `string`, or other runtime-managed type** — a bare type parameter whose constraints exclude class and interface substitutions (`where T: value`) included | **not applicable** | **not applicable** | **not applicable** | **not applicable** | outside this table; no obligation arises — and a **borrow-bearing** record, a borrow-bearing inline array, or a choice that holds borrows carries none either, its **carried borrows** being governed not here but by [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal)'s return bullet: receiver-sourced, static-storage-sourced, or null-source | [§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types), [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal) |
| 8 | **move-only value type** (an owning inline array; an owning-classified choice, case constructions included) | **Owned** move-only value | **Owned** | **Owned** | **Owned** | The caller discharges by binding into a local (auto-disposed at scope end), into an owning-inline-array slot, into a class field of move-only type (a value carrying no borrows only), or — for a choice — by a consuming match ([§35.5](#sec-owning-match)). A `Task<T>`/`OwningTask<T>` over such a `T` is rejected at the declaration ([§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal)). | *Producers*; [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types); [§35.4](#sec-choice-classification) |

Row 6's three *cannot arise* cells state a derived fact: every callee kind but the static one contributes a structural source, so the empty set arises only at static declarations — where the rejection is the sourceless-factory rule. Rows 2 and 3 differ in spelling only: the explicit marker changes nothing.

<a id="sec-argument-contributions"></a>
**The sources an argument contributes (derives: [K2.2](#sec-kernel-k2) + [K2.4](#sec-kernel-k2)).** Where a rule counts the sources a call's plain (non-`owned`) arguments contribute — to a function-value invocation's borrow (rows 4 and 5 above), to a `ref` or plain `out` location (*Borrow lifetime rules*' *A `ref` or plain `out` location outlives the call*), to a field-stored borrow (*Borrow lifetime rules*' field-store bullet, clause 2), or to a deferred-activation frame (*Deferred-activation callees*, *Returning a deferred-activation frame*, [§29.4](#sec-lazy-evaluation)) — it counts each argument by kind:

1. a class- or interface-typed argument contributes its source set;
2. a function-typed argument contributes its source set (*Borrow lifetime rules*' closure bullet); at a deferred-activation frame the count is the argument's **capture-set contribution** (*Deferred-activation callees*);
3. a borrow-bearing record or inline-array argument ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties)), or an argument of a choice type that holds borrows ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)), contributes the sources of the borrows it carries;
4. in a generic body, which is checked once under the weakest assumption its constraints establish ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2), an argument whose type is a type parameter, or whose borrow-bearing or holds-borrows classification turns on one, contributes at every substitution the union of what each substitution its constraints admit would contribute — at a type parameter admitting a class or interface substitution, what a class- or interface-typed argument contributes; under `where T: value`, the sources of the borrows it may carry;
5. an `owned` argument, and a `null`-literal, other value-typed or other runtime-managed argument, contributes nothing.

A rule that excepts an argument kind states the exception where it applies: the deferred-activation frame excepts a `CancellationToken`, whose source obligation is [§30.8](#sec-cancellation)'s.

<a id="sec-factory-methods-and-sourceless-returns"></a>
#### Factory methods and sourceless returns

A **static** method call has no structural borrow source: there is no receiver, and a static method may not re-expose static storage through a non-`owned` return (the property-getter-only admission, *Borrow lifetime rules* below). A non-`owned` class- or interface-typed static return therefore names no one responsible for the result, and the signature is **rejected at the declaration**:

A `static` method or `operator` declaration — wherever it occurs: a class, a `static` class ([§11.7](#sec-static-classes)), a record, an enum, or an interface's static member set ([§11.8](#sec-static-interface-members)) — whose declared return type is a class or interface type is a **compile error** unless the declared type itself announces the classification — the [announcement table](#sec-announcement-table)'s static column: `owned` (rows 1 and 3), a **mint-announcing** type (row 2), or a **bare type parameter** with a non-empty potential source set (row 5). An **empty-set** bare-type-parameter return is rejected exactly as a concrete class type is (rows 4 and 6): spell `owned T`, admissible over every constraint domain under [§28.1](#sec-where-the-owned-modifier-can-appear)'s per-instantiation erasure; a returned parameter whose constraints exclude class and interface substitutions (`where T: value`) is outside this rule entirely — no disposal obligation can arise at any admissible substitution, and §28.1 rejects the marker on such a declaration.

Every admissible static signature is therefore **type-announced**: the caller-side classification of a static call is read off the declared return type with no heuristic. The caller of an `owned`-returning static factory discharges the obligation under the standard rules (store in an `owned` field, bind with `using var`, transfer, consume as an unbound owned temporary, or explicitly dispose).

Instance methods are untouched by this rule. Outside the mint-announcing families (*Calls mint for the mint-announcing families* below), a non-`owned` class-typed instance return remains a borrow whose source is the receiver, and an instance method that produces a fresh value must declare `owned` — [§28.6](#sec-leak-prevention) rejects a freshly-produced owned value returned through a non-`owned` return. Documentation phrases like "returns a fresh instance" carry no weight in any classification; the qualifier in the signature — or the mint-announcing declared type — is the only transfer signal. *(Derivation — [K2.4](#sec-kernel-k2): every admissible static signature announces its result's classification — type-announced — and the callee-side borrow-return prohibition below rejects the unannounceable bodies; the two rules are opposite sides of one boundary and are enforced together.)*

**Calls mint for the mint-announcing families (derives: [K6.2](#sec-kernel-k6) + [K6.3](#sec-kernel-k6)).** The instance-method borrow classification above has one type-keyed exception, in clauses:

1. **The rule.** A **call** whose declared return type — read from the signature *before* generic substitution, with nullability stripped (`Task?`, `IEnumerable<T>?` qualify) — is a **mint-announcing type** produces an **owned** frame at the call site, at every callee kind — the [announcement table](#sec-announcement-table)'s rows 2–3, all four columns (interface dispatch classifies at the declaring signature: the table's inheritance rule).
2. **The set.** The mint-announcing types are the **`Task` family** (`Task`, `Task<T>`, `OwningTask<T>`) and the **iterable family** — the [§29.3](#sec-iterator-methods)/[§30.7](#sec-asynchronous-programming-async-iterators) iterable and enumerator interfaces (`IEnumerable<T>`, `IEnumerator<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerator<T>`, `IOwningEnumerable<T>`, `IOwningEnumerator<T>`, `IOwningAsyncEnumerable<T>`, `IOwningAsyncEnumerator<T>`) together with the **lazy query** ([§29.11](#sec-multiple-enumeration)). A lazy query's declared type is ordinarily a head already; where it is one of stdlib §5's derived interfaces instead (the `OrderBy`/`OrderByDescending`/`ThenBy`/`ThenByDescending` quartet's `IOrderedEnumerable<T>`; `GroupBy`'s result is head-typed — `IEnumerable<IGrouping<TKey, T>>` — and needs no separate reading), the operator is the same minting member by its lazy-query kind (compiler-known, as [§29.11](#sec-multiple-enumeration)'s provenance tracking already is), while the derived interfaces themselves stay outside the head set at every declared-type-keyed boundary (the static-announcement rule above, [§27.1.1](#sec-function-type-assignability), [§27.6](#sec-method-references)). The lazy query's single-consumption rule governs the frame's **enumeration right**, layered over — not identified with — the container obligation the standard rules discharge ([§29.11](#sec-multiple-enumeration)); it is no separate ownership regime.
3. **The announcement.** No factory warning is emitted — the declared type is the announcement (**type-announced**, [K6.2](#sec-kernel-k6)). The receiver is no borrow source for the container: a mint-announcing callee mints a fresh frame at every call (an `async` body's state machine, [§30.1](#sec-async-methods); an iterator body's state machine, [§29.3](#sec-iterator-methods); a composed operator result, stdlib §5) or forwards one it owns — `async` is an implementation-side modifier no signature or interface can expose ([§28.12](#sec-asynchronous-disposal)), and an iterator body is likewise invisible in the signature — and the disposal stories (`using var text := File.ReadAllTextAsync(path);`, [§30.1](#sec-async-methods); the `for` desugaring's `using var __source` over an iterable call, [§29.2](#sec-desugaring-of-for)) require the caller to hold the container obligation.
4. **Caller side.** The caller discharges the container obligation under the standard rules: bind it (a `using var` over such a call **assumes the disposal obligation** — an owned right-hand side, not a [§28.10](#sec-using-var-initialized-from-a-borrow) pin), transfer it, or consume it as an unbound owned temporary (*Unbound owned temporaries* below — the dominant `await Producer()` and `for var x in Producer() do … end` shapes). Reads of **storage** — a property, field, indexer, or local of such a type — are not calls and remain **borrows of their storage** ([K1.5](#sec-kernel-k1)). Orthogonally, the produced frame still *carries* the call's receiver's and plain arguments' borrows to its [K6.1](#sec-kernel-k6) bound — settlement for a task ([§30.1](#sec-async-methods)), completion or disposal for an iterator frame, the single consumption point for a lazy query — the deferred-activation classification (*Deferred-activation callees* below) unchanged.
5. **Callee side.** An unmarked mint-announcing return type is itself ownership-transferring for the container — the same announcement-by-declared-type logic as an `owned` return — so every return path of a non-`async`, non-iterator method or lambda with such a return type must supply a fresh or owned frame (an `async` or iterator body satisfies this automatically — its return *is* its own fresh state machine): any source an `owned` return admits — a forwarded mint-announcing call result, a completed-task factory result ([§30.10](#sec-standard-library-task-helpers)), an owned frame local or `owned` parameter, or a `move`d owned field of such a type; for a *nullable* mint-announcing return type, `null` remains admissible on any path (the caller's owned binding is then owned-currently-null — the producers-table null row). **One excluded source, for both families:** the invocation of a **call-bounded** plain function-typed parameter — the minted frame inherits the call bound and must be consumed to its [K6.1](#sec-kernel-k6) bound within the callee (a task awaited to settlement, and in a non-`async` body the invocation itself rejected; an iterable frame enumerated or disposed there — [§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters)); declare the parameter `scoped` or, for the task case, make the callee `async`.
6. **Borrow returns rejected.** Returning a **borrow** — a bare field or property read, a plain parameter, a captured binding — is a compile error (the [§29.1](#sec-iterator-protocol) self-returning enumerator's `return this;` is the one admitted receiver return, axiom [A15](#sec-axiom-register)), with the remedy named: a *stored* frame — a stored task, a stored collection view — is re-exposed through a **property, field, or collection slot**, whose reads are borrows of their storage ([§30.11](#sec-taskcompletionsourcet-and-ownedtaskcompletionsourcet)'s source-owns-task rule; [§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order)(b)'s cache read as `_cfg!`; the stored-view property face `public property Items: IEnumerable<Item> => _items;`, whose lend-only guarantee is axiom [A4](#sec-axiom-register)'s), or at a **concrete collection type**, whose non-`owned` instance return remains an ordinary receiver-sourced borrow — never through an unmarked mint-announcing method return.
7. **Function-type targets.** The same pre-substitution keying governs the rule's **callee side at a function-type target**: a lambda's admission is read against the target slot's declared, pre-substitution return type ([K2.4](#sec-kernel-k2)'s type-announced reading), never against the type an inference or an explicit substitution gives it. A slot whose declared return is a bare type parameter is therefore never mint-announcing at any instantiation: the lambda takes *Bare-type-parameter returns*' callee-side admission (below) — a capture- or plain-parameter-sourced borrow is admitted (`xs.Select(lambda(x) => x.Items)` over a property-face `Items` at `U = IEnumerable<Item>`), while a fresh frame is an owned production, rejected at the return path (`Wrap<IEnumerable<int>>(lambda() => Nums())` over a yield-based static `Nums`) — the inhabitant-side closure the iterable family carries in place of a per-substitution exclusion.
8. **Scope notes.** A generic method whose declared return type is a bare type parameter (`First<T>(): T`) is **not** classified by this rule at any instantiation — it is classified by *Bare-type-parameter returns* below, whose receiver-and-argument-sourced borrow is exactly the classification element and cache accessors over collections of tasks or iterables keep; frame-valued storage is consumed through its admitted borrow positions instead ([§30.5](#sec-result-lifetime-and-task-disposal); iterating a stored collection view borrows it as any other storage read). An explicit `owned` on a mint-announcing return remains admissible with identical semantics: the same contract stated with emphasis (`GetEnumerator(): owned IEnumerator<T>`, [§29.1](#sec-iterator-protocol); `Domain.Spawn(...): owned Task`, stdlib §6.8).

<a id="sec-bare-type-parameter-returns"></a>
**Bare-type-parameter returns (derives: [K2.4](#sec-kernel-k2); empty source set → rejected at the declaration — *Factory methods* above).** In clauses:

1. **The rule and its keying.** A **call** whose declared return type — read from the signature *before* generic substitution, with nullability stripped (`T?` qualifies; an `owned T` return is not bare — it is the ordinary ownership-transferring return, [§28.8](#sec-ownership-transfer)) — is a **bare type parameter** in scope at the callee's declaration (a method-, type-, or extension-block-level parameter) is classified by this rule at every call site and every instantiation, at every callee kind — the [announcement table](#sec-announcement-table)'s rows 5–6. The keying is pre-substitution, exactly as the calls-mint rule above — no type-keyed classification (that rule, or any future one) applies to such a call at any instantiation.
2. **Inheritance.** The classification is **inherited by implementations and overrides**: a method implementing or overriding a generic declaration whose return type is a bare type parameter carries this classification at every call site, direct or dispatched, exactly as the declaration's constraints are inherited ([§14.2](#sec-constraints-on-overrides)) — dispatch flows through the generic signature, so its classification is the only one call sites can be checked against. The potential source set is read from the **generic declaration's** signature, its source parameters identified positionally through the substitution (an implementing signature's own concrete types mention no type parameter, and a coincidentally same-typed non-source parameter is not a source); the callee-side check below is inherited the same way — an implementing or overriding body is checked under the same return-path admission, against the positionally corresponding source parameters and its own receiver.
3. **Scope.** A returned parameter whose constraints exclude class and interface substitutions (`where T: value`) is outside this rule on both sides.
4. **The potential source set.** The signature's potential source set is the call's receiver (for an extension method, the receiver parameter; for a function-value invocation, the function value), if any, together with every **plain** (non-`owned`) parameter whose declared type mentions the returned type parameter; `owned` parameters are never sources — they are consumed into the callee and die there.

**Caller side.**

1. With a **non-empty** potential source set, at a class or interface instantiation of the returned parameter the call produces a **borrow** carrying the **union of the source-liveness constraints** of the receiver and of every argument bound to a source parameter (at a function-value invocation, of the function value and of every plain argument, whatever its slot's type, each counted as [*The sources an argument contributes*](#sec-argument-contributions) counts it, as row 4 counts them: a lambda at a bare-return slot may return a borrow reached through any plain parameter of its own, *Calls mint for the mint-announcing families* item 7, so the function-typed narrowing of clause 2 reads a method's source parameters only) — the join machinery of the merge rules above: the result is usable only where every contributing source is still live. `Math.Max(a, b)` (stdlib §2.2) yields a borrow with sources `{a, b}` — the returned value *is* one of the caller's arguments, and neither side acquires a disposal obligation. No factory warning is emitted — the declared bare-type-parameter return is the announcement (**type-announced**, [K2.4](#sec-kernel-k2)). (The stdlib [§5](Bezel_Standard_Library.md#sec-system-collections-linq) class-element terminal accessors are this classification at its highest-traffic site; where such a result's receiver provenance roots at a same-unit fresh-yield iterator, the borrow is dead on arrival and the call draws [§29.11](#sec-multiple-enumeration)'s terminal-accessor provenance warning.)
2. A borrowed argument contributes its own carried constraints transitively; an argument that is an **unbound owned temporary** (a fresh producer, a `move` result — `Math.Max(move box.f, b)`) bounds the result borrow to the same full expression, and a binding, store, return, or other escape of the result past that expression is rejected ([§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal)'s reject-not-extend posture — the remedy names the source first); a null-literal argument, and any argument or receiver whose substituted type is a value type that carries no borrow, or a runtime-managed type other than a function type, contributes no constraint (a function-typed argument contributes as stated below) (in a generic body, an argument whose type is a type parameter, or whose borrow-bearing or holds-borrows classification turns on one, is read under the weakest assumption its constraints establish, [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2: it is excluded here only where every substitution its constraints admit is so excluded; a call all of whose contributing sources are null literals carries no constraint — any non-null value such a call can return must come from the callee's static-storage paths, which are process-lived). An argument or receiver whose substituted type is a borrow-bearing record or inline array, or a choice type that holds borrows ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)), contributes the sources of the borrows it carries: `static method Unwrap<T>(b: Box<T>): T => b.V;` over `record Box<T>(V: T)` lends, at `T = Item`, from what `b` carries. A function-typed argument bound to a source parameter whose declared type, nullability stripped, is a function type that mentions the returned parameter in its return slot or in a `ref` or `out` parameter slot, other than a slot declared `owned` (`f: () -> T`, `f: (T) -> T`, `f: () -> () -> T`, `f: (out T) -> bool`), and the function value of a function-value invocation, contribute their source sets ([§28.3](#sec-borrow-lifetime-rules)'s closure bullet): an invocation of such a value can hand the callee a borrow of the returned parameter's type that carries the value's set, as its result or through the `ref` or `out` location (*Borrow lifetime rules*' *A `ref` or plain `out` location outlives the call*), and the callee side's clause 2 admits that borrow as a return. `static method Apply<T>(f: () -> T): T => f();` therefore lends, at `T = Item`, from what its argument captures: the result of `Apply<Item>(lambda() => x)` is usable only where `x` is live. A function-typed argument whose declared type mentions the returned parameter only in parameter slots that are neither `ref` nor `out` (`First(predicate: (T) -> bool): T`), or only in slots declared `owned` (`GetOrAdd(key: K, factory: (K) -> owned V): V`), contributes no constraint: no invocation of it hands the callee a borrow of that type.
3. The result composes with the ordinary machinery unchanged: consuming a contributing source while the result borrow is live is rejected by the consume-site freeze below; an explicit `Dispose()` of a source remains the site-announced kill with the checked-mode backstop ([§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal)); every borrow-lifetime and escape rule applies. At a value or runtime-managed instantiation the result is not a borrow. At one that is a borrow-bearing record or inline array ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties)), or a choice type that holds borrows ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)), the borrows the result carries take clause 1's union, clause 2's temporary bound included, and [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal)'s rules read them: over `static method Id<T>(a: T): T => a;` and `record Pair(Item: Item)`, `return Id<Pair>(new Pair(x));` with `x` scope-bound is rejected at the return. At every other value or runtime-managed instantiation no constraint attaches ([§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types)).
4. With an **empty** potential source set — no receiver and no plain source parameter (`static method Create<T>(): T where T: new()`) — the call has no structural source at any call site and the signature is **rejected at the declaration** (*Factory methods* above) — spell `owned T`, the form the standard library itself uses for fresh-producing generic signatures: `OwningSet<T>.Pop(query: T): owned T` (stdlib §4.10, under `where T: class`) and the stdlib §2.19 producer members (`Zero(): owned T`, `Parse(s: string): owned T`), admissible over domains admitting value substitutions under [§28.1](#sec-where-the-owned-modifier-can-appear)'s per-instantiation erasure.

**Callee side.** The check is signature-keyed and decidable, and is enforced **per instantiation category** — the [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2 pattern that [§28.5](#sec-owned-fields)'s generic-field admissibility already uses — the diagnostic naming the instantiation ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 4):

1. At value and runtime-managed substitutions of the returned parameter the check is vacuous (returning a parameter copies the value — or moves it, for a move-only inline-array substitution, [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types) under [§14.2](#sec-constraints)'s instantiation-time move discipline), except at a substitution that is a borrow-bearing record or inline array, or a choice type that holds borrows: there clause 2's check and clause 4's rejections apply as at a class substitution, bounding the borrows the returned value carries, which the caller side's clause 3 counts.
2. At class and interface substitutions, with a **non-empty** potential source set, every return path must supply `null` or a borrow whose sources outlive the call: **the receiver** — directly or through the receiver's fields and indexers ([§28.6](#sec-leak-prevention)'s receiver-sourced notion);
