The clause is not admitted on a choice *case* (the case is the discriminant — skipping it is incoherent; a compile error, [§9.2](#sec-equality-skip)).

A choice that is **not** auto-hashable — any borrow-bearing or owning choice (class-typed payloads are outside the admissible-component rule, exactly as class-typed record fields are), any value-like choice with an inadmissible payload, and any choice carrying a homogeneous `=`/`<>` overload (the paragraph above) — draws [§9.2](#sec-body-records)'s **use-site compile error** on `=`, `<>`, direct `Equals`/`GetHashCode` calls, and — no default rendering being generated off the auto-hashable set either ([§8.5](#sec-tostring) carries the row) — a `ToString()` call at a statically-known receiver type, a choice-typed interpolation hole included; a **boxed** receiver's dispatched call cannot be rejected statically and renders the qualified type name, as a `T`-typed operand, an operand typed by a generic choice whose type arguments are or contain a type parameter (`Result<T, E>` in a generic body) and a component of a generated rendering do ([§8.5](#sec-tostring)). Each is drawn unless the author declares the member itself ([§9.2](#sec-body-records)'s per-member rule; for `=`/`<>`, the operators under [§25.2](#sec-operator-overloading-restrictions)'s co-declaration rule). Declaring the choice is fine; comparing it is the error, with the same remedies §9.2 names. The exemption for **direct `Equals`/`GetHashCode` calls** is keyed on the declared **members**, not on the operators: a choice that declares plain `Equals(other: C): bool` and/or `GetHashCode(): int` ([§35.2](#sec-choice-members)) admits **the declared member's** call on **every** classification, owning and borrow-bearing included — they resolve statically to the declared members, which is what §35.2's *reachable by static dispatch only* states. The exemption is therefore **per member**, its ground being per member: a choice declaring only `Equals(other: C): bool`, which [§8.3](#sec-equals-and-gethashcode)'s pairing leaves possible only on a choice owning at every instantiation, admits `.Equals(…)` and still draws the use-site error on `.GetHashCode()`, and conversely. No co-declared pair is required — [§25.2](#sec-operator-overloading-restrictions)'s co-declaration rule is keyed to **operators**, which this exemption explicitly is not. The `=`/`<>` half stays keyed on the operators, there being nothing for `a = b` to invoke without an overload ([§25.2](#sec-operator-overloading-restrictions)). Declaring the pair grants a **call**, not a property: the choice does not thereby become auto-hashable or **hashable** ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties)), and is no more usable as a hash-container key than before. A **boxed** receiver's `Equals` and `GetHashCode` are decided member by member, as [§9.2](#sec-body-records) decides a non-auto-hashable record's. Where the choice declares the member, the box reaches it: [§35.2](#sec-choice-members) carries [§10.5](#sec-restrictions)'s replacement rule to the boxable classifications in either spelling, so a declared `Equals(other: C)` fills the box's `Object` slot, and an argument that is not a boxed `C`, `null` included, compares unequal. Otherwise the box reaches the inherited `Object` member: `Equals` is reference equality of the two boxes, and `GetHashCode` is the box's identity hash, assigned as for a class instance ([§8.3](#sec-identity-hash-assignment)). No structural comparison or hash is synthesized for the boxed path. A `T`-typed operand is not a boxed receiver: its `Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `=` and `<>` uses are read at the substitution under [§9.2](#sec-equality-through-a-type-parameter)'s per-instantiation rule. *(This follows the record precedent, not [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)'s inline-array borrowing-equality precedent: reference equality smuggled inside a value type's `=` is virtually never the intended semantics — rationale [§9.6](Bezel_Design_Rationale.md#sec-choices-why-a-new-kind).)*

Value-like auto-hashable choices are **hashable** and usable as hash-container keys, as is a value-like choice that is outside auto-hashable only through its own homogeneous `=`/`<>` overload, on the strength of [§25.2](#sec-operator-overloading-restrictions)'s co-declared `Equals(T)`/`GetHashCode` — without that arm the co-declaration rule would oblige an author to declare an equality surface the language then refused to use; the other classifications are not ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties)'s hashable row, unchanged).

<a id="sec-choice-boxing"></a>
### 35.8 Boxing and interfaces

Boxing follows the classification, each arm riding an existing [§8.6](#sec-boxing) rule:

- **Value-like** choices box per the general rule; the box is runtime-managed.
- **Borrow-bearing** choices box under §8.6's borrow-bearing-record rules verbatim: the boxed copy carries the same borrows, extends no lifetime, and may not escape the sources' scopes.
- **Owning** choices **cannot be boxed** — §8.6's move-only rule, word for word: boxing copies, move-only forbids copying. A program that needs an owning choice's contents to cross a boxed-value boundary transfers the payloads out through a consuming match first.

A choice may declare interface conformance (interfaces only, as for records — [§9.6](#sec-records-and-inheritance), whose settable-member exclusion applies to choices identically, [§9.4](#sec-value-receivers-are-borrows)), providing matching public members per [§10.5](#sec-restrictions)'s enum model; [§14.2](#sec-constraints)'s conformance rule gains the corresponding choice clause. For an **owning-classified** choice the conformance declaration remains legal — constraint satisfaction and generic dispatch work without boxing — but the *conversion* of an owning value to an interface or `Object` type is rejected at the conversion site (it is a boxing, forbidden above). For a generic choice this is per-instantiation ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2): a conformance-declaring choice converts at value-like instantiations and rejects at owning ones.

`Dispose` stays off the surface everywhere: choices do not implement `IDisposable` ([§8.7](#sec-dispose-is-not-on-object)) — an owning choice's disposal obligation is discharged by its *holder* (scope end, owning field, consuming match), never by calling `Dispose()` on it, exactly as for owning inline arrays.

<a id="sec-choice-nullable"></a>
### 35.9 Nullable `C?`

`C?` is the ordinary nullable value type ([§7.2](#sec-nullable-value-types)): a `C?` scrutinee adds [§19.6](#sec-exhaustiveness)'s explicit-`null`-arm requirement on top of the choice clause; `?.`/`??`/narrowing compose as for any nullable; boxing strips the wrapper per [§8.6](#sec-boxing)'s nullable-value-type rule (for the boxable classifications).

For an **owning** `C`, the wrapper `C?` is itself move-only (it contains a move-only value), with two consequences: `null` assignment into an owned-state `C?` location is drop-on-overwrite — the displaced value's payloads are disposed ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)) — and `default(C?)` is a valid null move-only value, on the precedent of [§17.11](#sec-the-default-operator)'s owning-inline-array form. The polymorphic-null-state row of [§28.3](#sec-producers)'s producers table applies to `var x: C? := null;` unchanged.

<a id="sec-choice-default-with"></a>
### 35.10 `default`, `with`, and the small surface

- **`default(C)` is a compile error for every choice type** — no choice is **defaultable** ([§17.11](#sec-the-default-operator)'s [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) property). A sum yields no distinguished zero: electing the first-declared case would make program meaning depend on declaration order, and restricting eligibility to first-case-payload-free would make *eligibility* order-dependent, which is worse. The enum precedent (underlying-0 with a warning) does not transfer — an enum value *is* its integer ([§10.3](#sec-underlying-type)) and 0 exists whether or not named; a choice value is a case, and no case is distinguished. Consequences: choices never satisfy `where T: new()`'s value-type arm ([§14.2](#sec-constraints) keys it on `default`); `serialized skip` on a choice-typed component requires the nullable form ([§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis)'s skip rule reaches this by itself). Programs wanting an empty state declare a payload-free case and construct it explicitly, or use `C?`.
- **`with` does not apply to choices.** [§9.5](#sec-non-destructive-update-with) requires a record-typed source; a choice's payloads are not independently replaceable storage (replacing one field of `Failed` is constructing a new `Failed`). A `with` over a choice-typed source is a compile error naming the remedy (construct the case anew).
- `nameof(FetchOutcome.Failed)` yields `"Failed"` ([§17.9](#sec-the-nameof-operator)); `typeof(FetchOutcome)` is ordinary; `is`/`as` over choice types follow value-type rules ([§17.4](#sec-the-is-is-not-and-as-operators)) and are rarely useful — the static type is always exact, choices being sealed.
- The discard `_ := c;` on an owning-choice value follows [§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)'s move-only discard clause verbatim (disposes at end of statement).

<a id="sec-choice-generics"></a>
### 35.11 Generics

A choice may declare type parameters and constraints, as records do; payload fields may use the parameters. Classification is evaluated **per instantiation** under [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2, with the payload marker's meaning fixed by [§28.1](#sec-where-the-owned-modifier-can-appear)'s per-instantiation erasure: a choice with `Ok(owned value: T)` is value-like at `T = int` (marker erased, payload an admissible value) and owning at `T = Connection` (marker means owned). An *unmarked* bare-type-parameter payload is classification-neutral at value and runtime-managed substitutions and **borrow-carrying** at class and interface substitutions — the same reading as a concrete unmarked class payload, making the marked/unmarked split uniform at every level of genericity: unmarked class payload = borrow (borrow-bearing choice), marked = owned (owning choice).

Method bodies of a generic choice type-check once, against `this`-as-borrow ([§35.2](#sec-choice-members)), so their checking is classification-independent; classification-dependent *admissibility* rules — boxing conversions, sendability, equality, conformance conversion, [§19.3](#sec-patterns)'s write-point rule for a move-only payload binding of a type-parameter payload, [§22.3](#sec-ref-and-out-argument-locations)'s owned-state bound at a `ref` or `out` argument naming a location whose declared type is or contains a type parameter, and [§9.4](#sec-value-receivers-are-borrows)'s rejection of an `async` or iterator member call on a move-only receiver — are enforced at the instantiation or use site with [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2's diagnostics. Rendering is not among them: where an instantiation is not auto-hashable and the choice declares no `ToString`, a generic body that renders an operand typed by the choice at type arguments that are or contain a type parameter in scope renders the instantiated type's qualified name ([§8.5](#sec-tostring)). (The compiler-provided members of stdlib `Result<T, E>` are outside this check-once discipline — their bodies exist only where the members are admissible; [§35.2](#sec-choice-members)'s `this`-as-borrow rule is unchanged for them.)

The choice classification's per-instantiation *behavior* consequences (copy vs. move on assignment; disposal vs. none at scope end) fall under [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties)'s behavior-dispatch reservation as its second scoped exception: the dispatch is performed by the language on a language construct — derived from structure, identical for every user, with no user-programmable hook. Users still cannot write code conditioned on a type parameter's category.

**No variance.** Variance attaches to interface and function-type parameters only ([§12.9](#sec-variance), [§14.3](#sec-generics-variance)); choices, like records and classes, are invariant. A `Result<Derived, E>` is not a `Result<Base, E>`; the conversion is an explicit re-wrap by match.

<a id="sec-choice-sendability"></a>
### 35.12 Sendability

A choice is **sendable** ([§30.14](#sec-sendable-types)) iff it is value-like and every payload field's type is sendable — [§30.14](#sec-sendable-types)'s value-type rule read at a choice's own components: its classification condition spelled *value-like* ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)), its per-component condition spelled per payload field; a sendable choice crosses as a copy. Borrow-bearing choices are never sendable (they carry origin-domain borrows). **Owning choices are not directly sendable** — the §30.14 move-only exclusion, unchanged — but §30.14's transfer-closure rule 2 admits an owning-choice-typed field of a transfer-closed class when the choice **holds no borrows** ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)'s holds-borrows property — a held borrow is an origin-domain borrow, exactly as in a borrow-bearing choice) and **every payload field of every case is transfer-compatible** ([#3111](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3111)/[#3110](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3110)): an obligation-bearing payload recursively — an `owned` class payload by its class's sendability, an `owned` interface payload never (§30.14 rule 3's reasoning at the payload position — interface types are never sendable), an owning-inline-array payload by its element class's sendability (an interface element type, [§15.1.1](#sec-owning-inline-arrays), is never sendable), a nested owning-choice payload by this condition applied recursively, the same recursive reach as [§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)'s active-case disposal — and every other payload by its own type's sendability, so a function-typed payload disqualifies exactly as a function-typed field does under §30.14 rule 3; such a value crosses inside its owner's ownership tree, exactly as owning-inline-array fields do.

<a id="sec-choice-ffi"></a>
### 35.13 FFI and serialization

Choices are **not FFI-compatible** ([§32.5](#sec-ffi-compatible-types)): the honest C spelling of a sum — a tag plus a union, with the tag discipline by convention — carries real ABI questions (union layout, tag width, niche packing), and [§32.13](#sec-c-compatible-records)'s layout-promise machinery is the future home if demand materializes. The in-memory layout of a choice (tag and payload representation, niche packing) is implementation-defined; only the value-type semantics of this section are normative.

Serialization synthesis for value-like choices — the `$case`-discriminated object form — is specified in [§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis).

---

<a id="sec-appendix-a"></a>
## Appendix A: Grammar

This appendix gives an EBNF grammar for Bezel. The grammar is a guide to the language's syntax; it is not strictly LL or LR. Terminal symbols are quoted; nonterminals are written `LikeThis`. `?` denotes optional, `*` denotes zero-or-more, `+` denotes one-or-more, `|` denotes alternation, parentheses group.

Whitespace and comments are recognized by the lexer and may appear between any two tokens; they are not shown in the grammar.

**Shared-production over-admissions (index, not a rule).** Several productions are shared across declaration forms, so the grammar admits, in some slots, forms that a section of the main text rejects semantically. The table indexes the instances of that policy; each rejection is defined in the section cited, and this table states no new rule.

| Grammar slot | Admitted syntactically | Rejected semantically by |
|---|---|---|
| `Param` in a primary-constructor header (A.3) | `ref`/`out` parameters, and a function-typed `scoped` parameter | [§22.10](#sec-methods-and-constructors-primary-constructors) |
| `Param` in an operator declaration (A.4) | `ref`, `out`, `owned`, and `scoped` parameter modifiers | [§25.2](#sec-operator-overloading-restrictions) |
| `Param` in `async` methods, `async` lambdas, and iterator methods (A.4) | `ref`/`out` parameters | [§30.1](#sec-async-methods) |
| `readonly?` on body-bearing property and indexer forms (A.4) | `readonly` where the shape already expresses read-onlyness | [§23.2](#sec-expression-bodied-read-only-properties) |
| `GenericParam` variance markers (A.3) | `in`/`out` on a generic parameter of a class, record, method, or type alias | [§12.9](#sec-variance) |
| `Visibility?` on a nested-type declaration (A.4 `NestedTypeDecl`) | omission of the keyword (the shared slot is optional; a nested type must fill it) | [§11.6](#sec-nested-types) |
| `Visibility?` and `GenericParams?` in the A.3 productions reused by a local type declaration (A.6 `LocalTypeDecl`) | any visibility keyword, any generic parameter list (both slots must be empty) | [§21.10](#sec-local-type-declarations) |
| `move`-rooted positional forms in pattern-embedded expressions (A.7) | e.g. a range bound rooted at the identifier-operand `move x` | [§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression) / axiom [A7](#sec-axiom-register) (the marked named slot's own admission conditions: [§19.3](#sec-patterns), [§35.5](#sec-choice-matching)) |
| `Expression` in a contract clause or an invariant member (A.4 `ContractClause`, `InvariantDecl`) | `result` (an `Identifier`) and `old(E)` (an `Identifier` with a call suffix) — neither has a terminal of its own — in any clause | [§22.16](#sec-clause-evaluation): `result` is a compile error in a unit-typed member's clauses, in a constructor's clauses, and in any `requires` or `invariant` clause; `old(E)` has its keyword reading only within an `ensures` clause of a method and is rejected in an invariant member (the contextual-keyword readings are Appendix [B.2](#sec-contextual-keywords)) |
| `Member` in an enum or choice body (A.3 `EnumDecl`, `ChoiceDecl`) | every member kind `Member` admits beyond §10.4's list — instance fields; mutable or `scoped` static fields; constructors, static ones included; destructors; block-form, storage-backed, and `static` properties; indexers; nested types; `invariant` members; `virtual`, `abstract`, and `sealed override` on any member, and `override` on any member outside the `Object`-virtual trio (`Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `ToString`) | [§10.4](#sec-methods-properties-static-members) (the exhaustive admitted-member list) and [§10.5](#sec-restrictions); [§35.2](#sec-choice-members) for choices; `invariant` by [§22.16](#sec-contract-clauses), destructors by [§8.7](#sec-dispose-is-not-on-object) |
| `Member` in a record body (A.3 `RecordDecl`) | `virtual`, `abstract`, and `sealed override` on any member, and `override` on any member outside the `Object`-virtual trio (`Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `ToString`); destructors; `invariant` members | [§9.2](#sec-record-dispatch-modifiers) (*Dispatch modifiers on value kinds*); destructors by [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal); `invariant` by [§22.16](#sec-contract-clauses) |
| `EnumInheritance`'s first item (A.3) | a first item that is a type but not one of §10.3's eight integer types (`enum E: string`) — the production has one shape for both the explicit-underlying-type and the interfaces-only lists | [§10.3](#sec-underlying-type) |

The per-production comments in this appendix mark further, production-local instances of the same policy in place.

**Grammar-foreclosed prohibitions (index, not a rule).** The mirror case: several sections state, as rules, prohibitions the grammar already forecloses. Such a rule is stated **for the reader**, and the diagnostic is a **syntax error** rather than the cited section's own. The instances:

| Prohibition | Stated by | Foreclosed by |
|---|---|---|
| `step` in a `case` pattern | [§16.4](#sec-stride) | A.7 `RangePattern` (no step clause) |
| `async` on a constructor, destructor, or property/indexer accessor | [§30.1](#sec-async-methods) | A.4 `MethodDecl` and A.7 `LambdaExpr` (the only productions admitting `async`) |
| `equality skip` on a choice **case** (as opposed to a case *field*) | [§35.7](#sec-choice-equality) | A.3 `ChoiceCase` (no `EqualityClause` slot; `CaseField` has one) |

Like the table above, this one states no new rule.

<a id="sec-lexical"></a>
### A.1 Lexical

```ebnf
Identifier      ::= Letter IdentCont* | "_" IdentCont+
                              /* The bare single-character `_` is NOT an
                                 Identifier: it is lexed as its own reserved
                                 token — the discard (§1.3, §17.13, B.1) — and
                                 no Identifier production ever matches it.
                                 Identifiers may begin with or contain `_`
                                 (`_camelCase`, `_f`, `snake_case`); only the
                                 bare token is reserved. */
IdentStart      ::= Letter | "_"
IdentCont       ::= IdentStart | Digit
Letter          ::= /any Unicode letter/
Digit           ::= "0".."9"
HexDigit        ::= Digit | "a".."f" | "A".."F"

IntLiteral      ::= DecLiteral | HexLiteral | BinLiteral
DecLiteral      ::= Digit ("_"* Digit)* IntSuffix?
HexLiteral      ::= "0x" HexDigit ("_"* HexDigit)* IntSuffix?
BinLiteral      ::= "0b" ("0" | "1") ("_"* ("0" | "1"))* IntSuffix?
IntSuffix       ::= "L" | "U" | "UL" | "LU"   /* case-insensitive */

FloatLiteral    ::= DigitGroup "." DigitGroup Exponent? FloatSuffix?
                  | DigitGroup Exponent FloatSuffix?
                  | DigitGroup FloatSuffix
DigitGroup      ::= Digit ("_"* Digit)*
Exponent        ::= ("e" | "E") ("+" | "-")? DigitGroup
FloatSuffix     ::= "f" | "F" | "m" | "M"     /* m -> decimal */

CharLiteral     ::= "'" CharContent "'"
StringLiteral   ::= '"' StringContent* '"'
                  | '@"' VerbatimContent* '"'
InterpString    ::= '$"' (InterpPart | StringContent)* '"'
                  | '$@"' (InterpPart | VerbatimContent)* '"'
InterpPart      ::= "{" Expression ("," "-"? IntLiteral)? (":" FormatSpec)? "}"
```

`CharContent`, `StringContent`, `VerbatimContent`, and `FormatSpec` are not given productions; their content is described in [§18.3](#sec-character-literals), [§18.4](#sec-string-literals), [§18.5](#sec-interpolated-strings), [§18.6](#sec-verbatim-strings), and [§18.8](#sec-escape-sequences-non-verbatim) of the main text. Briefly: `CharContent` is one Unicode scalar value or one escape sequence; `StringContent` is any sequence of code points or escapes other than an unescaped `"` (inside an `InterpString`, `{{` and `}}` denote literal braces, a single `{` begins an `InterpPart`, and a single unescaped `}` that does not close a hole is a compile error); `VerbatimContent` is any sequence of code points other than `"`, with `""` denoting a single `"`; `FormatSpec` is a brace-free sequence of format characters, terminated by the hole's closing `}`, with the §18.5 top-level delimitation rule deciding where it begins. Its vocabulary and semantics are normative in stdlib §2.18.

<a id="sec-source-file"></a>
### A.2 Source file

```ebnf
SourceFile      ::= ModuleDecl Import* TopDecl*
ModuleDecl      ::= "module" QualifiedName ";"
Import          ::= "import" QualifiedName ("as" Identifier)? ";"
                              /* alias: a file-scoped qualifier for the
                                 imported module (§2.2). */
QualifiedName   ::= Identifier ("." Identifier)*

TopDecl         ::= ClassDecl | InterfaceDecl | RecordDecl | EnumDecl
                  | ChoiceDecl
                  | ExtensionDecl | TypeAliasDecl | ExternBlock
TypeAliasDecl   ::= "type" Identifier GenericParams? ":=" Type
                              /* The alias binds with `:=`, like every other
                                 binding. No Visibility alternative: a module-level alias
                                 is always module-internal (§27.8). */
                    GenericConstraints* ";"
```

<a id="sec-type-declarations"></a>
### A.3 Type declarations

```ebnf
ClassDecl       ::= Visibility? Modifier* "class" Identifier GenericParams?
                    PrimaryCtorParams?
                    Inheritance?
                    GenericConstraints*
                    ClassBody
PolymorphicMember ::= "polymorphic" "(" PolyCase ("," PolyCase)* ","? ")" ";"
PolyCase ::= StringLiteral ":" QualifiedName
                              /* A `polymorphic` registry is a class-body member
                                 (at most one per class; takes no visibility).
                                 Each PolyCase maps a wire discriminator string
                                 to a permitted concrete derived type. The set is
                                 closed and explicitly registered: there is no
                                 reflective discovery of subtypes (rationale
                                 §5.18, §5.22). The discriminator must be a
                                 non-empty literal and unique within the
                                 registry; each QualifiedName must name a type
                                 assignable to the declaring class and itself
                                 type-driven serialization-eligible (declares
                                 ISerializable/IDeserializable). The declaring
                                 base class may be concrete (it registers its own
                                 discriminator) or abstract (no self case).
                                 `polymorphic` is a contextual word here, not a
                                 reserved keyword. A class enters serialization
                                 synthesis by declaring ISerializable/IDeserializable;
                                 the serialized shape is read from its field
                                 types (§9.8), with no class-header clause. */
                              /* The grammar admits modifier combinations the
                                 type system rejects: `static class C(args)`
                                 parses (Modifier* allows `static`,
                                 PrimaryCtorParams? is optional and present)
                                 but is rejected semantically — static classes
                                 cannot be instantiated and so cannot carry
                                 primary-ctor parameters (§11.7). */
ClassBody       ::= Member* "end" Identifier? ";"
Modifier        ::= "abstract" | "closed" | "sealed" | "static"
                              /* Modifier* permits any combination; the
                                 semantically valid combinations are described
                                 in §11.7. `closed` (closed abstract class)
                                 combines with no other class-shape modifier:
                                 `closed abstract`, `closed sealed`, and
                                 `closed static` are rejected, as is
                                 `sealed abstract` (the
                                 diagnostic names `closed`); other combinations
                                 with `static` are rejected. */
PrimaryCtorParams ::= "(" ParamList? ")"
Inheritance     ::= ":" InheritItem ("," InheritItem)* ","?
InheritItem     ::= Type ("(" ArgList? ")")?
                              /* The grammar accepts the optional argument list
                                 on every InheritItem; semantically, the
                                 argument list is permitted only on the base
                                 class (the first item), not on interfaces. */

InterfaceDecl   ::= Visibility? "interface" Identifier GenericParams?
                    Inheritance?
                    GenericConstraints*
                    InterfaceMember* "end" Identifier? ";"

RecordDecl      ::= Visibility? "record" Identifier GenericParams?
                    PositionalFields?
                    Inheritance?
                    GenericConstraints*
                    ( ";" | RecordBody )
PositionalFields ::= "(" PositionalField ("," PositionalField)* ","? ")"
PositionalField ::= Identifier ":" Type SerializedClause? EqualityClause?
EqualityClause  ::= "equality" "skip"
                              /* Per-member exclusion from auto-equality
                                 (§9.2 "The `equality skip` clause"),
                                 mirroring SerializedClause: the marked
                                 storage component is removed from the
                                 §9.2 membership computation and cannot
                                 disqualify the record. `equality` is
                                 contextual (B.2), and within the clause
                                 `skip` is likewise contextual; only the
                                 skip form exists (no rename, no optional).
                                 Attached at PositionalField, the
                                 auto-property alternative of PropertyDecl
                                 (A.4), FieldDecl (A.4), and CaseField —
                                 in the fixed order SerializedClause?
                                 EqualityClause? where both slots exist
                                 (an arbitrary but stated order, keeping
                                 the grammar LL; each clause at most once).
                                 NOT on EnumConstant (an enum value is not
                                 a component) and NOT on ChoiceCase (the
                                 case is the discriminant); on computed
                                 properties, methods, and statics the
                                 clause is a compile error (§9.2's
                                 inert-annotation rule). */
SerializedClause ::= "serialized" ( "skip" | SerializedName )
SerializedName   ::= StringLiteral? "optional"?   /* at least one of the two
                                                     must be present */
                              /* Compiler-recognized field-name customization
                                 for serialization synthesis (§9.8). NOT an
                                 attribute system: a closed vocabulary, no
                                 user extensibility, no runtime introspection.
                                 `serialized "name"` renames; `serialized
                                 optional` makes the field tolerant
                                 (omit-if-null on write, default-if-missing on
                                 read); `serialized "name" optional` combines
                                 the two; `serialized skip` excludes the field
                                 and is mutually exclusive with a name or
                                 `optional`. `skip` and `optional` are
                                 contextual words here, not reserved keywords;
                                 the `SerializedName` form requires at least
                                 one of the string or `optional` (a bare
                                 `serialized` is a syntax error). */
RecordBody      ::= Member* "end" Identifier? ";"

EnumDecl        ::= Visibility? "enum" Identifier EnumInheritance?
                    EnumConstants
                    Member* "end" Identifier? ";"
                              /* the shared Member production; §10.4's
                                 admitted-member list and §10.5 reject the
                                 rest semantically — see the over-admission
                                 index. */
EnumInheritance ::= ":" InheritItem ("," InheritItem)* ","?
                              /* `enum E: int, IComparable<E>` (explicit
                                 underlying type, then interfaces) and
                                 `enum E: IComparable<E>` (default underlying
                                 type int, interfaces only) share one
                                 production: the first item is the underlying
                                 type iff it resolves to one of §10.3's eight
                                 integer types — keyword or reserved PascalCase
                                 alias — decided semantically, not by token
                                 class (§10.3). */
EnumConstants   ::= EnumConstant ("," EnumConstant)* ","? ";"
EnumConstant    ::= Identifier (":=" ConstExpr)? SerializedClause?
                              /* `serialized "name"` on an enum constant
                                 customizes that member's serialized name
                                 (§9.8). `serialized skip` and `serialized
                                 optional` are not admitted on enum constants
                                 — an enum value is a single member, not a
                                 field that can be omitted or defaulted; using
                                 them here is a compile error. */

ChoiceDecl      ::= Visibility? "choice" Identifier GenericParams?
                    Inheritance?
                    GenericConstraints*
                    ChoiceCases
                    Member* "end" Identifier? ";"
ChoiceCases     ::= ChoiceCase ("," ChoiceCase)* ","? ";"
ChoiceCase      ::= Identifier CasePayload? SerializedClause?
                              /* SerializedClause on a case admits the rename
                                 form only; `skip` and `optional` are rejected
                                 semantically, as on enum constants (§9.8). */
CasePayload     ::= "(" CaseField ("," CaseField)* ","? ")"
CaseField       ::= "owned"? Identifier ":" Type SerializedClause? EqualityClause?
                              /* The payload field form is PositionalField plus
                                 the optional leading `owned` marker; the
                                 marker's admissibility follows §28.1's type
                                 requirement, including the bare-type-parameter
                                 erasure. Inheritance names interfaces only
                                 (as for records). §35.1. */

ExtensionDecl   ::= Visibility? "extension" Type GenericConstraints*
                    ExtensionMember* "end" "extension"? ";"

ExternBlock     ::= "extern" StringLiteral ("convention" StringLiteral)?
                    ExternDecl+ "end" "extern"? ";"
ExternDecl      ::= Visibility? "method" Identifier "(" ExternParamList? ")"
                    (":" "owned"? Type)?
                    (":=" "symbol" StringLiteral VariadicClause?)? ";"
ExternParamList ::= ExternParam ("," ExternParam)* ","?
ExternParam     ::= Param | "env"
VariadicClause  ::= "variadic" "(" IntLiteral ")"
                              /* `owned` on the return marks ownership transfer
                                 per §32.6's contract (§28.1: owned returns are
                                 declared). `symbol`, `variadic`, and `env` are
                                 contextual (Appendix B.2). In ExternParam the
                                 parser distinguishes by two-token lookahead:
                                 `env` followed by `:` is an ordinary Param
                                 named `env`; a bare `env` is the user-data
                                 slot marker (§32.8). `env` also appears as a
                                 parameter-type atom inside a function-typed
                                 extern parameter (§32.8); the type grammar
                                 admits it there as an ordinary identifier and
                                 §32.8's pairing rules give it meaning — the
                                 over-admit-and-reject-semantically pattern.
                                 Param modifiers: `ref`/`out` admitted per
                                 §32.5's boundary rules; `owned`, `out owned`,
                                 and `scoped` rejected semantically. */
```

<a id="sec-members"></a>
### A.4 Members

```ebnf
Member          ::= FieldDecl | MethodDecl | PropertyDecl | IndexerDecl
                  | ConstructorDecl | DestructorDecl
                  | OperatorDecl | NestedTypeDecl | ConstDecl
                  | PolymorphicMember | InvariantDecl
ExtensionMember ::= MethodDecl | ExpressionPropertyDecl
                              /* `static` is rejected inside extension blocks
                                 (§26.3); MethodDecl's "static"?
                                 alternative does not apply here. */

InterfaceMember ::= IfaceMethod | IfaceProperty | IfaceIndexer
                  | IfaceStaticMethod | IfaceStaticOperator
IfaceStaticMethod   ::= "static" "pure"? "method" Identifier GenericParams?
                        "(" ParamList? ")" (":" "owned"? Type)?
                        GenericConstraints* ContractClause* ";"
                              /* same body slot as IfaceMethod (§22.16) */
IfaceStaticOperator ::= "static" "operator" OpToken
                        "(" ParamList? ")" (":" "owned"? Type)? ";"
                              /* §11.8: abstract-only — a body is an
                                 error; static properties/consts are
                                 deferred. Conformance and dispatch rules in
                                 §11.8. */
IfaceMethod     ::= "pure"? "method" Identifier GenericParams?
                    "(" ParamList? ")" (":" "owned"? Type)?
                    GenericConstraints* ContractClause* ";"
                              /* GenericConstraints* sits where MethodDecl's
                                 does, after the return type and before the
                                 clause region; a method implementing the
                                 member inherits its constraints (§14.2). */
                              /* clauses are self-delimited; the lone ";" is the
                                 uniform member terminator, clause-bearing or not
                                 (§22.16) */
                              /* `owned` on the return type follows the same
                                 rule as in MethodDecl. An interface declaring
                                 an `owned` return requires implementations to
                                 declare an `owned` return (§11.2's exact-match
                                 rule). */
IfaceProperty   ::= "pure"? "readonly"? "property" Identifier ":" Type
                    ( ";" | Accessor* "end" Identifier? ";" )
IfaceIndexer    ::= "pure"? "readonly"? "property" "[" ParamList "]" ":" Type
                    ( ";" | Accessor* "end" ";" )
                              /* The accessor-block form declares explicit get/set
                                 accessors (e.g. `get; set(owned);`) on an interface
                                 property or indexer; in interface context each
                                 Accessor uses the `;`-terminated AccessorBody (no
                                 implementation), enforced semantically. See §23.3. */
FieldDecl       ::= Visibility "static"? ("owned" | "scoped")? "readonly"?
                    EqualityClause? Identifier ":" Type (":=" Expression)? ";"
                              /* "scoped" fields (§28.14) hold storage-
                                 bounded callbacks: function-typed only,
                                 invocable/overwritable/clearable, never read
                                 out as an escaping value. */
                              /* EqualityClause here is the point of §9.2's
                                 clause: an explicit field is §9.2's
                                 disqualifier, and the clause is what
                                 un-disqualifies it (record bodies; on a
                                 class field, and on a static field
                                 anywhere, it is rejected semantically —
                                 §9.2). SerializedClause never appears on
                                 FieldDecl: explicit fields are not
                                 serialized components of a record
                                 (§9.8). */
ConstDecl       ::= Visibility "static"? "const" Identifier (":" Type)?
                    ":=" ConstExpr ";"

ContractClause  ::= "static"? ("requires" | "ensures") "(" Expression ")"
                              /* the parentheses are clause syntax, not expression
                                 tokens (§22.16): a clause is self-
                                 delimiting and carries no terminator. */
InvariantDecl   ::= "static"? "invariant" "(" Expression ")" ";"
                              /* class bodies only; rejected semantically in
                                 records and static classes (§22.16); the `;` is
                                 the ordinary member terminator. */
                              /* the clause region (§22.16): after the signature's
                                 GenericConstraints*, the tokens requires/ensures
                                 (or static followed by either) open it. The
                                 keyword reading is unconditional: requires,
                                 ensures, and invariant are reserved words
                                 (B.1), so no identifier reading exists
                                 anywhere, and the region ends at the first
                                 token that opens no clause. */

MethodDecl      ::= Visibility "static"? ("async" | "pure")? VirtualKind?
                    "method" Identifier GenericParams?
                    "(" ParamList? ")" (":" "owned"? Type)?
                    GenericConstraints* ContractClause*
                    MethodBody
                              /* clauses are self-delimited (§22.16); every
                                 MethodBody alternative, the lone ";" included, is
                                 reachable at any clause count */
                              /* The optional `owned` modifier on the return
                                 type marks methods whose result transfers
                                 ownership to the caller (§28.8). It applies
                                 to class-typed returns; for non-class types
                                 it is rejected semantically. */
VirtualKind     ::= "abstract" | "virtual" | "sealed"? "override"
MethodBody      ::= "=>" (Expression | AssignmentStmt) ";"
                              /* The AssignmentStmt alternative is
                                 valid only on methods with no declared return
                                 type (unit result); it makes the accessor
                                 shape `set => _x := value;` available to the
                                 identically-shaped unit method:
                                 `method SetX(v: int) => _x := v;` (§22.2).
                                 Enforced semantically. */
                  | Statement* "end" Identifier? ";"
                  | ";"                /* body-less method: requires
                                          VirtualKind = "abstract"; enforced
                                          semantically. Interface methods use
                                          IfaceMethod, not MethodDecl, so the
                                          ";" body here is exclusively for
                                          abstract members. */

PropertyDecl    ::= Visibility "static"? "pure"? VirtualKind?
                    "readonly"? "property" Identifier ":" Type
                    PropertyBody
PropertyBody    ::= "=>" Expression ";"
                  | AutoAccessorVis? (":=" Expression)? SerializedClause? EqualityClause? ";"   /* auto-property */
                              /* the two clauses in the fixed order shown,
                                 each at most once (A.3 EqualityClause). */
                  | Accessor* "end" Identifier? ";"
AutoAccessorVis ::= Visibility ("get" | "set")   /* e.g. `private set` */
Accessor        ::= Visibility? "pure"? "get" AccessorBody
                  | Visibility? "set" SetterParamSpec? AccessorBody
                              /* "pure" is admitted on "get" only — a "pure set"
                                 does not parse (the set alternative carries no
                                 "pure" slot); §22.15 states the rule */
SetterParamSpec ::= "(" "owned" ")"
                              /* Explicit setter parameter spec, used when
                                 the parameter modifier needs to be declared
                                 (typically `owned` for owned-element-collection
                                 indexer setters). The parameter is always
                                 named `value`, and its type is always the
                                 property's declared type, so neither is
                                 written here. When the SetterParamSpec
                                 is omitted (`set` alone), the
                                 implicit `value` parameter has no modifier
                                 and takes a borrow of the property's declared
                                 type (§22.3, §23.3). Only `owned` is
                                 meaningful on the value parameter: it is an
                                 input, so `ref`/`out` do not parse here. */
AccessorBody    ::= "=>" (Expression | AssignmentStmt | "do" Statement* "end") ";"
                  | ";"                                  /* abstract / interface body */
                              /* The single-statement form `set => _x := value;`
                                 (an AssignmentStmt) parallels the §13.6 prose; it
                                 is distinct from the expression form (assignment is
                                 a statement, not an expression) and the do-block
                                 form. */

IndexerDecl     ::= Visibility "static"? "pure"? VirtualKind?
                              /* "static" is over-admitted here and rejected
                                 semantically: indexers may not be static
                                 (§23.5). Parameter default values (":=" in
                                 the shared ParamList) are likewise
                                 over-admitted and rejected: indexer
                                 parameters may not declare defaults
                                 (§23.5). */
                    "readonly"? "property" "[" ParamList "]" ":" Type
                    PropertyBody
                              /* IndexerDecl reuses PropertyBody, whose block
                                 form is `Accessor* "end" Identifier? ";"`.
                                 The optional Identifier is for property
                                 declarations (matching the property's name);
                                 indexers have no name, so the only valid
                                 form for an indexer's block-form `end` is
                                 plain `end;`. Enforced semantically —
                                 IfaceIndexer states the same rule structurally
                                 in its bespoke body; this production's
                                 reuse-plus-semantic-rejection is the grammar's
                                 deliberate shared-production policy. */

ConstructorDecl ::= Visibility "pure"? "constructor" "(" ParamList? ")"
                    ContractClause*
                              /* the static-constructor alternative admits no
                                 "pure" (§22.15) and no clauses (§22.16) */
                    CtorChain? Statement* "end" "constructor"? ";"
                  | "static" "constructor" "(" ")"
                    Statement* "end" "constructor"? ";"
CtorChain       ::= ("base" | "this") "(" ArgList? ")" ";"

DestructorDecl  ::= "destructor" Statement* "end" "destructor"? ";"

OperatorDecl    ::= "public" "static" "pure"? "method" "operator" OpToken
                    "(" ParamList ")" ":" "owned"? Type OperatorBody
                              /* `owned` on an operator's return type is
                                 permitted for class-typed operators that
                                 allocate. Most operator overloads return
                                 records or value types and do not need it.
                                 ParamList is the shared production; parameter
                                 modifiers on operator parameters are rejected
                                 semantically (§25.2). */
OperatorBody    ::= "=>" Expression ";"
                  | Statement* "end" ("operator" OpToken)? ";"
OpToken         ::= "+" | "-" | "*" | "/" | "mod" | "&" | "|" | "^"
                  | "<<" | ">>" | "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">="
                  | "=" | "<>" | "~"

NestedTypeDecl  ::= ClassDecl | InterfaceDecl | RecordDecl | EnumDecl
                              /* The reused productions carry `Visibility?` for
                                 the top-level default-internal rule (§13.2).
                                 In nested position the visibility keyword is
                                 required (§13.3, §11.6); omission is
                                 rejected semantically. */

ParamList       ::= Param ("," Param)* ","?
Param           ::= ParamModifiers? Identifier ":" Type (":=" Expression)?
                    OutNullPostcond?
                              /* A method/constructor parameter cannot be named
                                 `_` — the bare token is not an Identifier
                                 (A.1), and the rejection diagnostic says why:
                                 parameter names are call-site-addressable API
                                 surface (§22.5, §2.8.2); choose a name
                                 (§17.13). Lambda parameters differ: LambdaParam
                                 (A.7) admits the bare-`_` ignore. */
                              /* `owned` precedes the identifier in every
                                 named-declaration position — Param, LambdaParam
                                 (via FuncParamMods, A.7), FieldDecl,
                                 CaseField; the post-colon
                                 spelling `x: owned T` does not parse (§28.1:
                                 the modifier attaches to the declaration, not
                                 the type). The pre-Type spelling ("owned"?
                                 Type) exists only in positions with no
                                 identifier — return types and FunctionType
                                 slots. */
OutNullPostcond ::= "when" ("true" | "false")
                              /* (§22.4): admitted only on `out` /
                                 `out owned` parameters of nullable type in
                                 bool-returning methods — a checked non-null
                                 postcondition tied to the stated result. No
                                 parse ambiguity: out parameters never carry
                                 defaults (§22.5), so the clause always
                                 directly follows the Type. */
ParamModifiers  ::= "ref"
                  | "out" "owned"?
                  | "owned"
                  | "scoped"
                              /* "scoped" is valid on function-typed
                                 parameters (§28.14: storage-bounded
                                 callback capture) and on class/interface-typed
                                 parameters (§28.14: storage-
                                 bounded borrow — scoped construction). On a
                                 static method it requires an `owned` return
                                 (§28.14). Other parameter types are
                                 rejected semantically. On a primary-
                                 constructor parameter only the class/
                                 interface-typed form is admitted (§22.10).
                                 Illegal on extern declarations (§32). */
ArgList         ::= Argument ("," Argument)* ","?
Argument        ::= ArgModifiers ArgExpression
                  | (Identifier ":=")? ArgExpression
                              /* ref/out/scoped arguments are positional-only
                                 (§22.5): the modifiers inhabit the first
                                 alternative, which has no named form. A
                                 move-rooted argument is an ordinary named or
                                 positional argument — the marker is part of
                                 the argument EXPRESSION, so `M(item := move x)`
                                 parses and is legal (§22.5). The
                                 operand category for ref/out arguments is
                                 semantic: §22.3 "ref and out argument
                                 locations". Named arguments are additionally
                                 rejected at the index position (§23.5) and at
                                 a call through a function-typed value (§27.1)
                                 — admitted by the shared grammar,
                                 rejected semantically. */
ArgModifiers    ::= "ref"
                  | "out" "var"?
                  | "out" "using" "var"
                  | "scoped"
                              /* No "owned" alternative exists (proposal 0090):
                                 the call-site transfer
                                 marker is part of the argument EXPRESSION —
                                 `M(move x)` parses through the plain
                                 ArgExpression path as an identifier-operand
                                 MoveExpr (A.7; §22.3, §28.8.1). An inline
                                 "out var" recipient adopts the resolved
                                 parameter's classification (§22.4); "out using
                                 var" is the scope-bound owned recipient,
                                 admitted only against an `out owned` parameter
                                 (§22.6). "scoped" (§22.3/§28.14) marks a
                                 class/interface-typed borrow argument to a
                                 `scoped` parameter — `M(scoped x)`; fresh
                                 producers rejected (§9.7). `scoped` remains an
                                 argument modifier: it marks a lending mode,
                                 not an action — the asymmetry with `move` is
                                 deliberate (§22.3). */
ArgExpression   ::= Expression | "_"
                              /* The "_" alternative is admitted by the grammar
                                 in any argument position and is the ONLY
                                 reading of `_` there — no Expression contains
                                 the bare token (A.1). It is semantically valid
                                 only when the corresponding parameter is `out`
                                 and the caller chooses to ignore the produced
                                 value (§22.4); in every non-out position —
                                 `ref _` included — it is a compile error
                                 (§17.13: a `ref` argument reads its operand,
                                 which a discard cannot supply). */


ExpressionPropertyDecl ::= Visibility "pure"? "readonly"? "property" Identifier ":" Type "=>" Expression ";"
                  /* the "readonly"? slot is a shared-production over-admission:
                     writing "readonly" on an expression-bodied property is
                     rejected semantically — §23.2's one-meaning rule (readonly
                     is written exactly where shape cannot express
                     read-onlyness, and an expression body already does). */


Visibility      ::= "public" | "internal" | "protected" | "private"

GenericParams   ::= "<" GenericParam ("," GenericParam)* ","? ">"
GenericParam    ::= Variance? Identifier
Variance        ::= "in" | "out"
                              /* Variance markers are semantically valid only on
                                 interface type parameters (§12.9; and not
                                 on interfaces declaring static members, §11.8).
                                 On class/record/method/alias parameters the
                                 marker is rejected semantically. */
GenericConstraints ::= "where" Identifier ":" Constraint ("," Constraint)* ","?
                              /* There is no `where T is owned` modifier-
                                 constraint form and no `<owned T>` generic
                                 argument (§14.4); constraints bound types
                                 only. */
Constraint      ::= "class" | "value" | "notnull" | "sendable" | "hashable" | "new" "(" ")" | Type
                              /* "new" "(" ")" is the parameterless-constructor
                                 constraint, three tokens with whitespace
                                 permitted (lexer-level) — `new()` and
                                 `new ()` are equivalent. */
```

<a id="sec-types"></a>
### A.5 Types

```ebnf
Type            ::= TypeNoNullable "?"?
TypeNoNullable  ::= QualifiedName GenericArgs?
                              /* Type arguments follow the last segment
                                 only, so no name here passes through a
                                 generic enclosing type: a type nested in
                                 one is named only where §2.7's
                                 enclosing-type lookup reaches it, or
                                 reaches a non-generic type enclosing it
                                 below the generic one (§11.6). */
                  | PrimitiveType
                  | InlineArrayType
                  | FunctionType
                  | "(" FunctionType ")"       /* parenthesized function type,
                                                  required before the `?`
                                                  nullable marker (§27.2):
                                                  `((int) -> bool)?`. In `-> T?`
                                                  the `?` binds to the return
                                                  type, not the function type. */
                  | "(" ")"                    /* unit type */
InlineArrayType ::= "[" ConstIntExpr "owned"? "]" Type
                              /* Inline array. Size must be a compile-time
                                 integer constant > 0. The optional `owned`
                                 marker (between size and closing bracket)
                                 marks slot ownership; the array becomes
                                 a move-only value type. See §15.1, §15.3.
                                 The inner Type is parsed greedily — `[3]int?`
                                 means an inline array of nullable int, not
                                 a nullable inline array. An inline array has
                                 no nullable form: a "null" inline array would
                                 have no natural representation (§15.1). */
ConstIntExpr    ::= Expression           /* a §17.14 constant expression of
                       integer type; see §15.1 "Size" */
GenericArgs     ::= "<" GenericArg ("," GenericArg)* ","? ">"
GenericArg      ::= Type
                              /* `owned` is not admitted on
                                 generic type arguments; the owned-bearing
                                 collection and task types are separate named
                                 classes (`OwningArray<T>`, `OwningTask<T>`, etc.).
                                 See §14.4. */
FunctionType    ::= "(" (FuncParamType ("," FuncParamType)* ","?)? ")" "->" "owned"? Type
                              /* The optional `owned` on the return marks
                                 a function type whose result transfers
                                 ownership to the caller. See §28.1. The
                                 `owned` is part of the function type's
                                 identity: `() -> Connection` and
                                 `() -> owned Connection` are distinct types. */
FuncParamType   ::= FuncParamMods? (Identifier ":")? Type
FuncParamMods   ::= "ref" | "scoped"
                  | "out" "owned"?
                  | "owned"
                              /* Same set as the method-declaration ParamModifiers
                                 (§A.4); function types and method declarations
                                 share modifier syntax exactly. The `out owned`
                                 combination represents an out-parameter that
                                 produces an owned value. */
IntegerType     ::= "byte" | "sbyte" | "short" | "ushort"
                  | "int" | "uint" | "long" | "ulong"
PrimitiveType   ::= IntegerType | "float" | "double" | "decimal"
                  | "bool" | "char" | "string"
                              /* The primitive KEYWORD spellings are tokens, not
                                 identifiers (§1.4, §3.4), so `var x: int` and
                                 `int.Parse(s)` need this production; the
                                 PascalCase aliases (`Int32`, `String`, …) arrive
                                 through QualifiedName as ordinary identifiers. */
```

<a id="sec-appendix-a-statements"></a>
### A.6 Statements

```ebnf
Statement       ::= LocalDecl | LocalConstDecl | AssignmentStmt | ExpressionStmt
                  | DiscardStmt
                  | IfStmt | WhileStmt | ForStmt | DoEndBlock
                  | CaseStmt
                  | ReturnStmt | ThrowStmt | BreakStmt | ContinueStmt
                  | TryStmt | YieldStmt
                  | IncrementStmt
                  | LocalTypeDecl

LocalTypeDecl   ::= RecordDecl | EnumDecl
                              /* Method-local type declaration (§21.10):
                                 `record`/`enum` are reserved and begin no other
                                 statement — token-one commit, no existing program
                                 changes meaning. The reused A.3 productions are
                                 restricted semantically: the Visibility? slot must
                                 be empty (a local type has no access surface —
                                 contrast §11.6, where nested types REQUIRE the
                                 keyword) and the GenericParams? slot must be empty
                                 (v1). Scope: the declaration to the innermost
                                 enclosing block's end, like a local variable
                                 (§21.6); order-significant (no forward references);
                                 no signature positions; no shadowing of a visible
                                 type name (§21.10). References to enclosing generic
                                 parameters are rejected (v1, §21.10). A.3
                                 (RecordDecl, EnumDecl) is unchanged. */

CaseStmt        ::= "case" Expression "of" CaseArm ("," CaseArm)* ","? "end" "case"? ";"
                              /* The statement form of §19's construct:
                                 `end`-terminated, with the statement's `;`
                                 following the closer. Arms use the same CaseArm
                                 grammar as the A.7 atom, and here
                                 ArmBody additionally admits its Statement and
                                 `do … end` alternatives; an expression-bodied
                                 arm's value is discarded per §21.9, applied per
                                 arm. The scrutinee has no `"owned"?` marker
                                 (proposal 0090): the scrutinee
                                 transfer marker is an ordinary scrutinee
                                 Expression whose root is an identifier-operand
                                 MoveExpr — `case move x of` — under §35.5's
                                 rules, identical to the atom's. */

LocalDecl       ::= "var" Identifier (":" Type)? (":=" Expression)? ";"
                  | "using" "var" (Identifier | "_") (":" Type)? ":=" Expression ";"
                  | "await" "using" "var" (Identifier | "_") (":" Type)? ":=" Expression ";"
                              /* `var _ := e;` does not parse as a LocalDecl —
                                 `_` is not an Identifier (A.1) — and is
                                 rejected with the two-remedy diagnostic:
                                 `_ := e;` (end of statement) or
                                 `using var _ := e;` (scope end) — §17.13,
                                 §21.1. The `"_"` alternative on the using-var
                                 forms is the anonymous owning binding
                                 (§17.13, §28.10): scope-end disposal, no name
                                 bound. Its `(":" Type)?` ascription slot is
                                 retained (`using var _: Stream := e;`) — the
                                 no-annotation rule governs the bare ignores,
                                 not this binding. */
                              /* The `await using var` form is admitted by the
                                 grammar at any LocalDecl position; it is
                                 valid only inside `async` methods and `async`
                                 lambdas, enforced semantically (§28.12,
                                 Appendix C.6). The binding-position
                                 transfer marker is the identifier-operand
                                 MoveExpr (A.7) at RHS root: `var y := move x;`
                                 is the MoveExpr as the entire RHS; admission
                                 is positional, enforced
                                 semantically (§28.3). A
                                 LocalDecl with neither a type ascription nor an
                                 initializer is rejected semantically (nothing
                                 determines the type; typed uninitialized locals
                                 follow §7.9's assignment-before-read rules). */

LocalConstDecl  ::= "const" Identifier (":" Type)? ":=" ConstExpr ";"
                              /* Initializer classified per §21.1:
                                 a §17.14 constant expression of primitive or
                                 string type is a compile-time constant;
                                 anything else is a runtime const. ConstExpr
                                 remains Expression, restricted semantically. */
                                /* local const; no visibility or static modifier */

AssignmentStmt  ::= LValue AssignOp Expression ";"
                              /* The assignment-position transfer marker
                                 is the identifier-operand MoveExpr (A.7) at
                                 RHS root: `y := move x;`. Valid only with ":=";
                                 admission is positional, enforced semantically
                                 (§28.3). */
AssignOp        ::= ":=" | "+=" | "-=" | "*=" | "/=" | "mod=" | "&=" | "|="
                  | "^=" | "<<=" | ">>=" | "??="
                              /* `mod=` is one token, lexed by longest match:
                                 the keyword `mod` immediately followed by `=`
                                 with no intervening space. `x mod = y` remains
                                 a syntax error. */
LValue          ::= Identifier | "this"
                  | LValue "." Identifier
                  | LValue "[" ArgList "]"
                              /* LValues have a restricted shape: the base must
                                 be `Identifier` or `this`, and only `.field`
                                 and `[index]` accesses extend the chain.
                                 Method-call results cannot serve as the base
                                 of an assignment; `getCache().items[0] := v`
                                 does not parse. Such cases require extracting
                                 the call result into a local variable first:
                                 `var c := getCache(); c.items[0] := v;`. */

DiscardStmt     ::= "_" ":=" Expression ";"            /* explicit discard */

IncrementStmt   ::= LValue ("++" | "--") ";"
ExpressionStmt  ::= Expression ";"

IfStmt          ::= "if" Expression "then" Statement*
                    ("elif" Expression "then" Statement*)*
                    ("else" Statement*)?
                    "end" "if"? ";"
                              /* every statement-level closer
                                 may optionally repeat its introducing keyword,
                                 checked when present — one uniform end-label
                                 rule (§1.6). */

LoopLabel       ::= Identifier ":"
                              /* only loop statements take a loop label.
                                 The Identifier closer alternative below is
                                 admitted grammatically on every loop and
                                 checked per §1.6: it must equal the loop's
                                 label; on an unlabeled loop an identifier
                                 closer is rejected, and on a labeled loop the
                                 keyword closer is rejected (the construct is
                                 named). No parse ambiguity: no statement
                                 begins Identifier ":" (":=" is one lexeme), and
                                 after "Identifier :" the parser requires "for",
                                 "while", or "await" "for". */

WhileStmt       ::= LoopLabel? "while" Expression "do" Statement*
                    "end" ("while" | Identifier)? ";"

ForStmt         ::= LoopLabel? "for" "var" (Identifier | "_") (":" Type)? "in" Expression
                    "do" Statement* "end" ("for" | Identifier)? ";"
                  | LoopLabel? "await" "for" "var" (Identifier | "_") (":" Type)? "in" Expression
                    ("with" Expression)? "do" Statement* "end" ("for" | Identifier)? ";"
                              /* The `"_"` alternative is the loop-variable
                                 ignore (§21.4, §17.13): binds nothing. The
                                 grammar over-admits the ascription on it;
                                 `for var _: T in …` is rejected semantically —
                                 a bare ignore takes its type from context,
                                 never an annotation (§17.13). */

DoEndBlock      ::= "do" Statement* "end" "do"? ";"

ReturnStmt      ::= "return" Expression? ";"
ThrowStmt       ::= "throw" Expression? ";"
BreakStmt       ::= "break" Identifier? ";"
ContinueStmt    ::= "continue" Identifier? ";"

TryStmt         ::= "try" Statement* CatchBlock FinallyClause? "end" "try"? ";"
                  | "try" Statement* FinallyClause "end" "try"? ";"
CatchBlock      ::= "catch" CatchArm ("," CatchArm)* ","?
CatchArm        ::= CatchPattern ("when" Expression)? "=>" ArmBody
CatchPattern    ::= Type ("|" Type)*                          /* no binding */
                  | "var" Identifier ":" Type ("|" Type)*      /* binding */
                              /* Multi-type alternatives are `|`-separated
                                 — the same alternatives
                                 spelling as case patterns (AltPattern). */
FinallyClause   ::= "finally" Statement*

YieldStmt       ::= "yield" "return" Expression ";"
                  | "yield" "break" ";"
```

<a id="sec-expressions"></a>
### A.7 Expressions

The grammar shown here is informal: it lists the alternatives at each precedence level rather than expanding every binary level into recursive productions. Operator precedence is given in [§17.1](#sec-precedence).

```ebnf
Expression      ::= LogicalOr
                  | ThrowExpr
                              /* IfExpr and CaseExpr are PrimaryAtom
                                 forms (self-delimited, usable in any operand
                                 position); no conditional level exists in the
                                 operator table (§17.1). A bare ThrowExpr
                                 appears at Expression top level and, because an
                                 atom's branches and arm bodies derive full
                                 Expressions, in any branch or arm body (§20). */
ThrowExpr       ::= "throw" Expression?
                              /* Bare "throw" (no operand) is valid only inside a
                                 catch arm body; outside a catch arm body, the
                                 operand is required. Enforced semantically. */
LogicalOr       ::= LogicalAnd ("or" LogicalAnd)*
LogicalAnd      ::= NullCoalesce ("and" NullCoalesce)*
NullCoalesce    ::= Equality ("??" (ThrowExpr | NullCoalesce))?
                              /* The right operand may be a throw expression —
                                 `x ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(…)`
                                 (§17.12); ThrowExpr is bottom-typed there. */
Equality        ::= Relational (("=" | "<>") Relational)*
Relational      ::= BitwiseOr (RelTail)*
RelTail         ::= RelOp BitwiseOr
                  | TypeRel TypeOperand
RelOp           ::= "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">=" | "in"
TypeRel         ::= "is" "not"? | "as"
TypeOperand     ::= Type | "null"
                              /* "is", "is not", and "as" take a Type on the
                                 right so that generic type arguments parse
                                 correctly: `x is Array<int>` parses with
                                 `Array<int>` as a Type, not as the bitwise
                                 expression `Array < int >`. The `null`
                                 alternative covers `is null` and `is not null`
                                 (§17.4); `as null` is a type error caught
                                 semantically. The other relational operators
                                 (`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `in`) take ordinary
                                 expressions and use RelOp. */
BitwiseOr       ::= BitwiseXor ("|" BitwiseXor)*
BitwiseXor      ::= BitwiseAnd ("^" BitwiseAnd)*
BitwiseAnd      ::= RangeExpr ("&" RangeExpr)*
RangeExpr       ::= Shift                                    /* no range */
                  | Shift (".." | "..<") Shift ("step" Shift)?
                                                             /* closed: a..b, a..<b,
                                                                with optional step */
                  | Shift ".."                               /* low-only: a..  */
                  | (".." | "..<") Shift                     /* high-only: ..b, ..<b */
                  | ".."                                     /* fully open: ..  */
                              /* Range bounds parse as Shift expressions, so
                                 `0..n+1` and `1<<2..1<<10` parse correctly,
                                 while `score in 60..100` and `r = 0..10`
                                 parse with the range as the right operand
                                 of the looser `in`/`=` operator. The open-
                                 ended forms support pattern matching (`..<0`
                                 matches values less than 0, `31..` matches
                                 values at or above 31; §19.3) and array
                                 slicing (`arr[..5]`, `arr[10..]`, `arr[..]`;
                                 §16.2). `step` is admitted only on closed
                                 ranges; open-ended ranges have no enumerable
                                 step semantics. */
Shift           ::= Additive (("<<" | ">>") Additive)*
Additive        ::= Multiplicative (("+" | "-") Multiplicative)*
Multiplicative  ::= UnaryExpr (("*" | "/" | "mod") UnaryExpr)*
                              /* The binary-level productions above derive the
                                 operator-category mixes that §17.2's mandatory-
                                 parenthesization rules reject (bitwise↔equality/
                                 relational/logical, shift↔additive, range↔bitwise);
                                 such a mix parses and is then rejected post-parse,
                                 enforced semantically per §17.2. */
UnaryExpr       ::= ("+" | "-" | "not" | "~") UnaryExpr
                  | "await" UnaryExpr
                  | PrimaryExpr
                              /* Right-recursive: `not not x`, `- -x` (with the
                                 space; `--` lexes as the decrement token), and
                                 `-(await x)` without parens all derive, matching
                                 §17.1 level 2's right-to-left associativity. */
PrimaryExpr     ::= PrimaryAtom PrimarySuffix*
PrimarySuffix   ::= "." Identifier GenericArgs?
                  | "?." Identifier GenericArgs?
                              /* The optional GenericArgs supplies explicit
                                 method type arguments at a call site:
                                 `obj.Method<int>(args)`. The GenericArgs
                                 belong to the member name; a following
                                 `"(" ArgList? ")"` suffix is the call.
                                 Same "generic arguments in an expression"
                                 family as the PrimaryAtom `Identifier
                                 GenericArgs?` form below. See §22.12. */
                  | "[" ArgList "]"
                  | "(" ArgList? ")"
                  | "?(" ArgList? ")"
                  | "!"
                  | "with" "(" InitAssign ("," InitAssign)* ","? ")"
                              /* The `with` suffix is the record copy-with-
                                 overrides expression (§9.5). It requires a
                                 record-typed source; a class-typed source is
                                 rejected semantically (§9.5), and so is a
                                 constructor-only record source, which is not
                                 defaultable and admits no `with` (§9.9) — the
                                 grammar over-admits and the type checker
                                 rejects, the same pattern A.4 uses throughout. */

PrimaryAtom     ::= Literal
                  | PrimitiveType
                              /* A primitive keyword in expression position:
                                 static access `int.Parse(s)` / `int.MaxValue`
                                 (§3.4) and the cast-call `int(d)` (§5.2). When a
                                 name in this position is followed by `?(`, the
                                 type reading wins: `T?(x)` where T resolves to a
                                 type is the §5.3 nullable cast, not a §7.6
                                 null-conditional call. */
                  | Identifier GenericArgs?
                              /* The optional GenericArgs lets a generic type
                                 name appear in receiver/expression position so
                                 its static members can be accessed with the type
```
