```ebnf
                                 arguments supplied — `Registry<int>.Register()`,
                                 `Cache<string>.Default`. Without a trailing
                                 member-access (or call) suffix, a bare
                                 `Identifier GenericArgs` is not a complete
                                 expression. The `<` that opens GenericArgs here
                                 is the well-known generics-vs-less-than ambiguity;
                                 the parser admits the GenericArgs reading only
                                 when the `<…>` is balanced and followed by a
                                 token that can continue a primary expression
                                 (`.`, `?.`, `(`, `[`), otherwise `<` is the
                                 relational operator. See §22.12. */
                  | "(" Expression ")"
                  | NewExpr
                  | MoveExpr
                  | LambdaExpr
                  | IfExpr
                  | CaseExpr
                  | BindExpr
                  | "this" | "base"
                  | NameOfExpr | TypeOfExpr | DefaultExpr
                  | CollectionLiteral
                  | "(" ")"                             /* unit value */

MoveExpr        ::= "move" PrimaryExpr
                              /* The PrimaryExpr operand must resolve to one
                                 of three things (§28.8.1); the shapes given
                                 are the spellings that reach them, and a
                                 trailing null-forgiving `!` suffix is
                                 TRANSPARENT here — `move _f!`, `move this._f!`,
                                 `move obj.f!` are the moves of the underlying
                                 field, §28.8.1's nullable-field detach
                                 (`move _slot!` then `_slot := null`; §17.8:
                                 `!` "does not move, copy, or borrow beyond
                                 what reading `x` already does"). The three:
                                 (a) an `owned` field of a class instance —
                                 spelled `Identifier` alone (the implicit-`this`
                                 abbreviation, `move _f`), `"this" "."
                                 Identifier`, or `PrimaryExpr "." Identifier`
                                 (`move obj.f`; field paths `move x.f.g`
                                 likewise); (b) a slot of an owning collection —
                                 `PrimaryExpr "[" ArgList "]"`
                                 where the receiver is an owning collection
                                 admitting slot-level move (`OwningArray<T>`,
                                 `OwningDictionary<K, V>`, `OwningBuffer<T>`
                                 for class-typed T, `Span<T>` over class-typed
                                 `OwningBuffer<T>`, or an owning inline array
                                 `[N owned]…`); or (c) a bare Identifier naming
                                 a local binding or `owned` parameter — the
                                 K3.4 transfer marker (proposal
                                 0090). Alternative
                                 (c)'s admission is positional, enforced
                                 semantically (§28.3): the entire RHS of a
                                 binding or assignment (a BindExpr clause's RHS
                                 included), an argument root (`M(move x)`,
                                 §22.3; named or positional alike, §22.5), a `case`
                                 scrutinee root (§35.5), an if-expression
                                 branch, or an expression-`case` arm
                                 result. Everywhere else — `??` operands,
                                 operator operands, guards, nested
                                 subexpressions — it is a compile error naming
                                 axiom A7's narrowed bound; at a marker-free
                                 position (`return`/`throw` operands, the
                                 discard RHS, owned-slot stores, a Pattern B
                                 `await` operand (§30.5), an owning iterator's
                                 `yield return` operand — in a borrowing
                                 iterator the position carries §29.2's
                                 recorded no-marker bound) it is rejected as
                                 redundant, the diagnostic naming the
                                 announcement (§28.3). The bare-Identifier
                                 spelling belongs to (a) or to (c) by what the
                                 name RESOLVES to — an `owned` field of the
                                 enclosing class is (a), a local binding or
                                 `owned` parameter is (c) — and the two are
                                 disjoint; only (c) carries the positional
                                 admission and the redundancy rejection above,
                                 a field move being the operative verb at every
                                 position (a plain field read never consumes,
                                 K9.1) and never redundant. Any other operand
                                 is a compile error. See §28.8.1 and §28.11. */

NewExpr         ::= "new" Type "(" ArgList? ")"
                  | "new" "(" ArgList? ")"              /* shorthand */
                              /* `new T(...) with(X := 5)` is parsed as
                                 `NewExpr` followed by a `with` PrimarySuffix;
                                 there is no separate ObjectInit production.
                                 The suffix is the record `with` of §9.5:
                                 legal when the constructed type is
                                 record-typed, rejected semantically
                                 when it is a class (§9.5) and when it is a
                                 constructor-only record (§9.9) — the two
                                 rejections the PrimarySuffix comment above
                                 states. */
InitAssign      ::= Identifier ":=" Expression

LambdaExpr      ::= "async"? "lambda" "(" LambdaParams? ")"
                    (":" Type)? "=>" LambdaBody
                              /* Keyword-led (§27.3): `lambda` is
                                 reserved and begins no other expression or
                                 statement, so the reading commits at the
                                 first token (the second, after `async`) —
                                 no scan to the matching `)` is ever needed,
                                 and a parenthesized construct followed by
                                 `=>` (a when-guard arm, a grouped
                                 expression) is never a lambda prefix. The
                                 parameter parens are mandatory, including
                                 the empty pair. The optional `":" Type` is
                                 the return-type ascription (§27.3); no Type
                                 production contains `=>` (function types
                                 use `->`), so the ascription ends
                                 deterministically before the arrow. */
LambdaParams    ::= LambdaParam ("," LambdaParam)* ","?
LambdaParam     ::= FuncParamMods? Identifier (":" Type)?
                  | "_"
                  | LambdaDestructure
                              /* The bare `"_"` alternative is the parameter
                                 ignore (§27.3, §17.13): accepted, binds
                                 nothing, contributes its slot to the function
                                 type; duplicate `_` parameters are legal
                                 (nothing is named). No FuncParamMods and no
                                 annotation compose with it — a typed ignore
                                 slot is spelled by the target type (§27.4). */
LambdaDestructure ::= QualifiedName "(" LambdaSlot ("," LambdaSlot)* ","? ")"
LambdaSlot      ::= Identifier | "_" | LambdaDestructure
                              /* Positional-record destructuring in parameter
                                 position (§27.4): irrefutable
                                 binding form only — the head names the
                                 parameter's exact positional-record type; no
                                 modifiers, no annotation, no refutable
                                 pattern elements. */
LambdaBody      ::= Expression
                  | "do" Statement* "end"

IfExpr          ::= "(" "if" Expression "then" Expression
                    ("elif" Expression "then" Expression)*
                    "else" Expression ")"
                              /* The conditional atom (§20). The
                                 parentheses are part of the form: in atom-start
                                 position, "(" followed by the reserved "if"
                                 commits the reading at the second token; in
                                 call/index-argument position the atom supplies
                                 its own pair. Each condition and branch derives
                                 a full Expression (a bare throw branch is
                                 admitted anywhere); "else" is mandatory. */
CaseExpr        ::= "(" "case" Expression "of" CaseArm ("," CaseArm)* ","? ")"
                              /* The expression-position case atom: arms
                                 are Expression-bodied only (ArmBody's Statement
                                 and do-block alternatives belong to the A.6
                                 CaseStmt). "(case" commits at the second token —
                                 "case" begins no other expression. */
                              /* The scrutinee has no `"owned"?` marker
                                 (proposal 0090). The scrutinee
                                 transfer marker (§35.5) is an ordinary scrutinee
                                 Expression whose root is an identifier-operand
                                 MoveExpr — `(case move x of …)`: admitted only
                                 when the scrutinee names a named owned binding
                                 of owning-choice classification; anywhere else
                                 it is a compile error. */
                              /* The scrutinee Expression is mandatory. `of`
                                 delimits the scrutinee from the first arm, so
                                 the scrutinee is a FULL Expression — no
                                 precedence restriction, no parenthesization
                                 rule — and a first pattern may begin with `-`,
                                 `..`, `..<`, or a relational token without
                                 ambiguity. */
CaseArm         ::= AltPattern ("when" Expression)? "=>" ArmBody
AltPattern      ::= Pattern ("|" Pattern)*
                              /* Pattern ALTERNATIVES are `|`-separated: the comma is exclusively the arm/slot
                                 separator, so no `=>` lookahead is needed and
                                 alternatives are available per positional slot
                                 (see PositionalPattern). `|`-joined members must
                                 be binding-free: constants, payload-free choice
                                 case names (§35.5), ranges, or
                                 relationals (§19.3). `|` never collides with
                                 bitwise-or (PatternBound below). */
BindExpr        ::= "(" BindClause+ Expression ")"
BindClause      ::= "var" Identifier (":" Type)? ":=" Expression ";"
                              /* The binding atom (§17.15): "(" followed
                                 by the reserved "var" — which begins no other
                                 expression — commits the reading at the second
                                 token, like the other paren atoms. Each clause
                                 introduces one single-assignment binding, in
                                 scope for the later clauses and the body; the
                                 ";" terminates the clause (no expression
                                 contains a top-level ";"). The body is one full
                                 Expression and supplies the atom's value and
                                 type. Clause initializers admit the marked
                                 transfer `move x` (a K3.4 binding transfer,
                                 §28.3); the body position does not. */
ArmBody         ::= Expression
                  | Statement                  /* valid only in a CaseStmt (A.6)
                                                  or in a catch arm; reads as a single
                                                  statement whose terminating `;` ends the
                                                  arm body, the same as `do Statement end` */
                  | "do" Statement* "end"     /* type (); valid only in a CaseStmt
                                                  or in a catch arm */
Pattern         ::= "_"                       /* discard */
                  | "null"                     /* null literal pattern */
                  | "var" Identifier (":" Type)?      /* binding */
                  | Constant                          /* single constant; `|`
                                                         alternatives live in
                                                         AltPattern above */
                  | RangePattern                      /* closed, half-open, or
                                                         open-ended range */
                  | RelOpPattern Shift                 /* relational; restricted
                                                         operator set, see below */
                  | Type                              /* type test */
                  | QualifiedName "(" (PositionalPatternList | NamedPatternList) ")"
                                                                /* destructuring */
                              /* The grammar does not syntactically distinguish
                                 a single-Identifier `Constant` (an enum
                                 constant or named const reference) from a
                                 single-Identifier `Type` (a type test): both
                                 productions match `Dog`. Disambiguation is
                                 by name resolution: if `Dog` resolves to a
                                 type, the pattern is a type test; otherwise
                                 it is a constant pattern. The same rule
                                 applies to QualifiedNames — `Color.Red` is a
                                 constant pattern; `System.IO.Stream` is a
                                 type-test pattern. */
PositionalPatternList ::= PositionalPattern ("," PositionalPattern)* ","?
PositionalPattern     ::= AltPattern              /* per-slot alternatives
                                                    :
                                                     TwoColor(Red | Blue, var x) */
                        | Identifier              /* naked binding,
                                                     valid only inside
                                                     positional destructuring */
NamedPatternList ::= NamedSlot ("," NamedSlot)* ","?
NamedSlot        ::= ("move")? Identifier "=" AltPattern
                              /* Named-destructure slots: a destructure's
                                 slot list is positional OR named, never mixed
                                 (v1, enforced structurally). After
                                 QualifiedName "(", an Identifier followed by "="
                                 commits the named reading — "=" is not a pattern
                                 relop (RelOpPattern below) and cannot occur in
                                 a pattern-embedded expression (PatternBound
                                 below). The optional
                                 "move" marks the slot:
                                 admitted only in an owning match, on an
                                 `owned`-marked payload field or a payload field
                                 of move-only value type, with a binding RHS —
                                 §19.3 (enforced semantically).
                                 `move Identifier "="` commits the
                                 marked reading — a three-token commit parallel
                                 to the named form's own two-token commit: "="
                                 cannot continue a pattern-embedded expression
                                 (above), and the `move`-rooted positional forms
                                 that do parse (a range bound rooted at the
                                 identifier-operand `move x`) are
                                 §28.8.1-rejected, so the marked
                                 slot displaces no accepted program. The slot
                                 Identifier is a plain member name (a qualified
                                 name before "=" does not parse). The slot RHS is
                                 a full AltPattern (per-slot alternatives,
                                 nesting); a naked identifier RHS resolves as at
                                 top level (constant or type test), never as a
                                 binding — a named-slot binding is spelled `var x`
                                 (§19.3). A constant slot is the "=" equality test
                                 (§8.4). Name resolution (records: storage
                                 fields/auto-properties; choice cases: payload
                                 field names; classes: public readable
                                 properties), the borrow-only unmarked-binding
                                 rule, and the marked slot's admission: §19.3;
                                 coverage: §19.6. */

RangePattern    ::= PatternBound (".." | "..<") PatternBound
                  | PatternBound ".."
                  | (".." | "..<") PatternBound
                  | ".."
PatternBound    ::= "-"? Shift
                              /* Dedicated pattern-position range form (mirrors RelOpPattern): no bare-expression
                                 leg (a lone Shift is not a range pattern) and no
                                 `step` (patterns test written bounds; stride has no
                                 membership meaning, §16.4). Bounds admit a
                                 leading `-` for negative literals. The
                                 scrutinee's type must be a §16.3 range `T`
                                 (§19.3). Every pattern-embedded expression —
                                 a range bound here, a relational operand
                                 (RelOpPattern Shift) — is a Shift production
                                 (§17.1), below `|` and `=`: a `|` at pattern
                                 level is always an alternative separator, and
                                 no pattern-interior expression can absorb a
                                 named slot's "=" (§19.3). */
RelOpPattern    ::= "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">="
                              /* Pattern-form relational operators are restricted
                                 to the four ordering operators. `is`, `is not`,
                                 and `as` are not pattern relops because they
                                 belong to TypeRel and take a Type rather than
                                 a value on the right. `in` is also excluded:
                                 a membership test against a collection or range
                                 is expressed with a Range pattern (`0..10`) or
                                 a Constant pattern with alternatives, not as
                                 a relational pattern. */
                              /* The Expression on the right of a RelOpPattern
                                 must have the same type as (or be implicitly
                                 convertible to) the scrutinee's type; the type
                                 check is semantic. The grammar admits more
                                 expression forms than the rule allows — for
                                 example, `< 60..100` parses but is rejected
                                 semantically because `<` between a value and
                                 a range is not defined. The scrutinee's type
                                 must have an intrinsic ordering (§19.3). */

CollectionLiteral ::= "[" (Expression ("," Expression)* ","?)? "]"
                    | "[" DictEntry ("," DictEntry)* ","? "]"                   /* dictionary */
DictEntry         ::= Expression ":" Expression

NameOfExpr      ::= "nameof" "(" QualifiedName ")"
TypeOfExpr      ::= "typeof" "(" Type ")"
DefaultExpr     ::= "default" "(" Type ")"
```

<a id="sec-constants-and-literals"></a>
### A.8 Constants and literals

```ebnf
Literal         ::= IntLiteral | FloatLiteral | CharLiteral
                  | StringLiteral | InterpString
                  | "true" | "false" | "null"
ConstExpr       ::= Expression           /* §17.14 constant expression */
Constant        ::= "-"? (IntLiteral | FloatLiteral)
                  | CharLiteral
                  | StringLiteral | "true" | "false" | "null"
                  | QualifiedName        /* enum constant, choice case (§35.5), or const reference */
```

`Literal` is the form referenced by `PrimaryAtom`; it includes interpolated strings since they are expressions. `Constant` is the restrictive form used in `case` patterns **only**; it omits `InterpString` (interpolated strings are not compile-time constants) and adds `QualifiedName` for enum constants and named constant references. `ConstExpr` is an `Expression` restricted semantically to the compile-time constant expressions of [§17.14](#sec-constant-expressions), which defines the admissible forms and the compile-time evaluation, including its faults.

---

<a id="sec-appendix-b"></a>
## Appendix B: Reserved Words

<a id="sec-reserved-keywords"></a>
### B.1 Reserved keywords

The following identifiers are keywords. Most are reserved unconditionally and may not be used as user-defined names. The **contextual keywords** (`convention`, `env`, `equality`, `get`, `hashable`, `notnull`, `of`, `old`, `operator`, `polymorphic`, `pure`, `result`, `scoped`, `sendable`, `serialized`, `set`, `step`, `symbol`, `value`, `variadic`) have keyword meaning only in specific syntactic positions and may be used as identifiers elsewhere; see [§B.2](#sec-contextual-keywords).

**Unconditionally reserved:**

`abstract`, `and`, `as`, `async`, `await`, `base`, `bool`, `break`, `byte`, `case`, `catch`, `char`, `choice`, `class`, `closed`, `const`, `constructor`, `continue`, `decimal`, `default`, `destructor`, `do`, `double`, `elif`, `else`, `end`, `ensures`, `enum`, `extension`, `extern`, `false`, `finally`, `float`, `for`, `if`, `import`, `in`, `int`, `interface`, `internal`, `invariant`, `is`, `lambda`, `long`, `method`, `mod`, `module`, `move`, `nameof`, `new`, `not`, `null`, `or`, `out`, `owned`, `override`, `private`, `property`, `protected`, `public`, `readonly`, `record`, `ref`, `requires`, `return`, `sbyte`, `sealed`, `short`, `static`, `string`, `then`, `this`, `throw`, `true`, `try`, `type`, `typeof`, `uint`, `ulong`, `ushort`, `using`, `var`, `virtual`, `when`, `where`, `while`, `with`, `yield`. (`requires`, `ensures`, and `invariant` are unconditionally reserved rather than contextual; the reservation closes the clause region's statement-stealing collision, proposal 0055 §3, so that nothing in a body's first-statement position can be *named* like a clause opener.)

**Contextual (see [§B.2](#sec-contextual-keywords)):**

`convention`, `env`, `equality`, `get`, `hashable`, `notnull`, `of`, `old`, `operator`, `polymorphic`, `pure`, `result`, `scoped`, `sendable`, `serialized`, `set`, `step`, `symbol`, `value`, `variadic`.

All keywords are lowercase. Type identifiers in PascalCase (`Object`, `Array`, `Type`, `Exception`, `IDisposable`, `Task`, etc.) are not keywords; they are names defined by the standard library or by compiler intrinsics.

**The reserved token `_`.** The bare underscore is reserved as a **token**, not as a keyword in the word sense: it is held out of the identifier namespace like a punctuation symbol — the discard/wildcard of [§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_) — and can never be declared or read as a name ([§1.3](#sec-identifiers)). Identifiers merely containing underscores are unaffected. (Holding a token out of the identifier namespace so a form stays re-introducible or unambiguous is [§B.3](#sec-future-reservations)'s existing discipline; `_` is that discipline applied permanently.)

<a id="sec-contextual-keywords"></a>
### B.2 Contextual keywords

The following keywords from [§B.1](#sec-reserved-keywords) carry meaning only in specific syntactic positions and may also appear as identifiers in other positions. The compiler distinguishes by context.

| Keyword | Reserved context | May be used as identifier |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | The `where T: value` constraint; the implicit setter parameter | Anywhere else: as a property name, a parameter name, etc. |
| `notnull` | The `where T: notnull` constraint | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `step` | After a range expression | Anywhere else |
| `convention` | After the library name in an `extern` block header | Anywhere else |
| `get`, `set` | Property and indexer accessor declarations (block form) and auto-property accessor visibility shorthand | Anywhere else |
| `operator` | After `static method` in an operator overload declaration | Anywhere else |
| `serialized` | The `serialized` clause on a positional field, auto-property, or enum constant (field-name customization, [§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis)). Within that clause, `skip` and `optional` are likewise contextual and are not reserved | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `equality` | The `equality skip` clause on a positional field, auto-property, explicit record field, or choice payload field (per-member auto-equality exclusion, [§9.2](#sec-equality-skip)). Within that clause, `skip` is likewise contextual and is not reserved — exactly `serialized`'s row | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `polymorphic` | The class-body `polymorphic (…)` registry member (class serialization synthesis, [§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `of` | The scrutinee/arm delimiter in a `case` expression ([§19](#sec-the-case-construct)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `scoped` | The storage-bounded modifier on a function-typed parameter or field, on a class/interface-typed borrow parameter, and its call-site argument marker ([§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters), [§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `symbol` | The `:= symbol "…"` alias clause of an extern declaration ([§32.11](#sec-symbol-binding)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `variadic` | The `variadic(N)` clause after an extern symbol alias ([§32.11](#sec-symbol-binding)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `sendable` | The `where T: sendable` constraint ([§14.2](#sec-constraints)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `hashable` | The `where T: hashable` constraint ([§14.2](#sec-constraints)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `pure` | The member-modifier slot ([§11.5](#sec-modifier-order), [§22.15](#sec-pure-members)) and the `pure get` accessor form | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `old` | Inside `ensures` clauses, where followed by `(` ([§22.16](#sec-clause-evaluation)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `result` | Throughout `ensures` clauses — the keyword reading always wins there; a parameter named `result` is not denotable in an `ensures` clause (rename it; `out`-parameter renames are call-site-invisible, [§22.5](#sec-optional-parameters-and-named-arguments)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier |
| `env` | The user-data slot marker in an extern parameter list and the corresponding position in an extern callback's function type ([§32.8](#sec-callbacks)) | Anywhere else: as an identifier — including as an extern parameter **name** (`env: IntPtr`; the following `:` disambiguates, grammar A.3). Inside an extern callback's **function type** the marker reading always wins: a user type named `env` is not denotable in that one position (rename or alias the type) |

The setter parameter is always named `value` ([§23.3](#sec-block-form-properties)). It is not a true keyword in that role: it is a parameter of the setter, and [§21.1](#sec-variable-declarations)'s *Local names* applies to it as to any other parameter.

`when`, `where`, `with`, and `yield` are reserved everywhere — although they appear only in specific syntactic positions in practice, the grammar treats them as full keywords for clarity. `when` has exactly two positions — the arm guard of a `case`/`catch` arm ([§19.4](#sec-guards)) and the `when true`/`when false` clause of an `out` parameter ([§22.4](#sec-out-nullability-postcondition)); it begins no expression and no statement, and a `when`-led expression or statement is a syntax error. `requires`, `ensures`, and `invariant` are in that category too: the words appear only in the clause region and the member-leading `invariant` position, but reserving them unconditionally makes the end of a clause region a fact about the *token*, not about what a body's first statement happens to be named — a body's first statement can no longer be a call to something named `requires`, so the clause region can never absorb a statement (proposal 0055 §3's first-statement collision, closed). `old` and `result` stay contextual: they are clause-interior names whose ordinary-identifier use (`result` especially) is common vocabulary, and their marker-wins rows above already resolve them without a seam.

<a id="sec-not-vs-notnull"></a>
#### `not` vs `notnull`

`not` (boolean negation, [§6.5](#sec-bitwise-operations)) is unconditionally reserved; it cannot appear as an identifier in any position. `notnull` (the generic constraint, [§14.2](#sec-constraints)) is contextual; it is reserved only in the `where T: notnull` position and may otherwise be used as an identifier (a parameter name, a field name, etc.). The two are distinct tokens — there is no relationship between their lexical statuses despite the visual similarity.

The two-token sequence `is not` ([§17.4](#sec-the-is-is-not-and-as-operators), type test combined with negation) is recognized by the parser specifically in the relational position; it does not require `not` to be contextual. `is not` parses as a single relational operator wherever a relational operator is expected, and `not` outside that two-token sequence remains the unary boolean operator. So `x is not Foo` and `not (x is Foo)` are both legal expressions with the same truth value but different narrowing behavior ([§17.4](#sec-the-is-is-not-and-as-operators)).

<a id="sec-future-reservations"></a>
### B.3 Future reservations

This version of the language reserves exactly one identifier for future use: **`event`**. It was the keyword of the retired event member kind ([§24](#sec-events)); it is held out of the identifier namespace so that pre-retirement declarations fail with a reserved-word diagnostic rather than parsing `event` as an identifier, and so that a one-line declaration form remains re-introducible without a breaking change. Any other new keywords in future revisions will be drawn from new compound forms or from words not currently used as identifiers in the standard library.

---

<a id="sec-appendix-c"></a>
## Appendix C: Compiler-Enforced Invariants

This appendix consolidates the invariants the compiler enforces. It is a checklist for implementers and a reference for programmers wanting to know which classes of error are caught at compile time.

<a id="sec-appendix-c-type-system"></a>
### C.1 Type system

- Every variable, field, parameter, and return value has a declared or inferred type.
- The bare token `_` is never a declarable or readable name ([§1.3](#sec-identifiers)): every declaration or read position naming `_` outside [§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)'s sanctioned discard/wildcard forms, the anonymous owning binding ([§28.10](#sec-using-var)), and the annotation-free ignores ([§27.3](#sec-lambda-expressions), [§21.4](#sec-the-for-statement)) is a compile error drawing the remedy-naming diagnostic of [§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_)'s rejected-positions list.
- Implicit conversions occur only as listed in [§5.1](#sec-implicit-conversions).
- When more than one overload is applicable to a call only because arguments match through different [§5.1](#sec-implicit-conversions) conversions, the call resolves to the unambiguously better candidate or is a compile error citing the candidates — the exact-match preference, the defaulted-arity tie-break, and the explicit-cast remedy are [§22.6](#sec-implicit-conversion-ranking)'s, mirrored for method references at [§27.6](#sec-method-references-to-overloaded-methods).
- A reference to a generic type — class, interface, record, or generic `type` alias — supplies exactly the declared number of type arguments; a bare name and a miscounted list are both compile errors naming the declared arity ([§14.1](#sec-generic-declarations), [§27.8](#sec-type-aliases)).
- Generic-method type arguments are inferred per [§14.5](#sec-type-argument-inference) — explicit lists all-or-nothing, exact agreement per parameter, second-phase lambdas, target-type completion, a failed inference making the candidate inapplicable, class/record/interface-level arguments never inferred from constructor arguments — with [§22.6](#sec-overloading)'s non-generic-over-generic comparison last before ambiguity.
- A choice declares at least one case; case names are distinct, do not collide with member names, and are never `Equals`, `GetHashCode` or `ToString` at any classification ([§35.1](#sec-choice-declaration)); a choice has no destructors, constructors, instance fields, storage-backed properties, indexers, or nested types; a choice type does not contain itself through value-typed components ([§35.1](#sec-choice-declaration)).
- `default(C)` is a compile error for every choice type C; choices never satisfy `where T: new()` ([§35.10](#sec-choice-default-with), [§14.2](#sec-constraints)).
- A `where` clause on a member declaration may constrain only that member's **own** type parameters: a clause whose *constrained* parameter is a type parameter of the **enclosing** declaration is a compile error. A clause constraining the member's own parameter is unaffected, including where its **bound** names an enclosing parameter (`method M<U>() where U: T` on `class C<T>` — [§14.2](#sec-constraints)'s *Type-parameter bounds*) ([§14.2](#sec-conditionally-admitted-members)).
- The names in one type-parameter list are distinct, and a generic method's type parameter does not reuse the name of a type parameter in scope at its declaration, including its enclosing type's or its generic extension block's ([§14.1](#sec-generic-declarations)).
- A non-nullable reference may not be assigned `null`.
- A nullable value may not be dereferenced without a null check or `!`.
- No operator lifts over a nullable operand: an operand of nullable type at an arithmetic, bitwise, shift, or relational (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) operator — built-in or user-declared, in expression, compound-assignment ([§6.6](#sec-compound-assignments)), or `++`/`--` ([§17.6](#sec-the-increment-and-decrement-operators)) position — is a compile error naming the [§7.4](#sec-member-access-on-nullable-values)/`??`/`!` remedies ([§7.11](#sec-lifted-operators), [§4.6](#sec-string)); a relational or range **pattern** requires a non-nullable scrutinee ([§19.3](#sec-patterns), [§16.6](#sec-empty-ranges-and-equal-bound-ranges)). Equality (`=`, `<>`, [§8.4](#sec-=-and)) and the marked propagating forms (`?.`, `?(args)`, `??`, `??=`) are unaffected, as are the other operators [§17.1](#sec-precedence)'s precedence table groups in the same band — the type tests `is`, `is not`, `as` ([§12.7](#sec-type-tests-is-is-not-as)) and `in` ([§17.5](#sec-the-in-operator)) — whose nullability behaviour is stated by, or derived at, their own sections — note that `in` states no rule of its own and takes the admissibility of the `Contains` call it is ([§17.5](#sec-the-in-operator)), which **does** reject a nullable left operand over any range.

- Every field of **non-defaultable** type is assigned in every constructor or has a field initializer; a field of defaultable type satisfies the rule vacuously, holding that type's default ([§7.9](#sec-definite-assignment-for-non-nullable-fields)).
- Every local of **non-defaultable** type is assigned before its first read, and a lambda body reads a captured local or `out` parameter only where it is definitely assigned at the lambda's formation (the target of the assignment whose whole right-hand side is the lambda counting as assigned) or by the body itself, a write in the body assigning it nowhere outside the body ([§27.5](#sec-closures)); a local of defaultable type declared without an initializer holds that type's default ([§7.9](#sec-definite-assignment-for-non-nullable-fields)).
- Definite-assignment analysis applies uniformly to instance and static non-nullable reference fields. A static constructor body's `try`/`catch` is subject to the same flow analysis as any constructor body: every path through the static initializer (including catch-and-recover paths) must definitely-assign every non-nullable reference static field.
- A type's `Equals` override requires a matching `GetHashCode` override; on an enum or a choice either spelling is the override, except on a choice owning at every instantiation ([§8.3](#sec-equals-and-gethashcode)).
- A class with one or more `abstract` members must itself be `abstract` (or `closed`, [§11.7](#sec-static-classes)).
- An abstract or `closed` class cannot be instantiated with `new`.
- Member hiding is forbidden: a derived class cannot reuse the name of an inherited member **visible at its declaration site** unless overriding a virtual member ([§12.2](#sec-hiding-is-not-allowed) — an invisible base member (`private`, or cross-module `internal`) does not block the name; the two are then distinct members with no override or overload relationship). A `Serialize` or `Deserialize` synthesized for the derived class's own serialization conformance is exempt; one it hand-writes where a base's member of that name is synthesized is not ([§9.8](#sec-serialization-synthesis)).
- An override must match the base member's visibility, return type, parameter types, **and parameter modifiers (`ref`, `out`, `owned`, `scoped`)** exactly, except that a parameter may widen `T` to `T?` ([§12.1](#sec-members-are-non-virtual-by-default) — the same contravariant allowance as interface implementations); the widening is monotone down the override chain. An override, and a member implementing an interface member, declares as many type parameters of its own as the declaration it matches, the two lists corresponding by position, not by name ([§11.2](#sec-interface-declaration), [§12.1](#sec-members-are-non-virtual-by-default)).
- An inheritance cycle is rejected: no type may, directly or transitively, list itself among its base classes or extended interfaces ([§12.10](#sec-inheritance-cycles)).
- A type may not declare two members indistinguishable under [§22.6](#sec-overloading)'s rules — nor may a non-overloadable member (field, property, nested type) share its name with any other member — the clash rejected at the second declaration ([§11.3](#sec-member-body)).
- A method-local `record`/`enum` declaration is an ordinary nominal record/enum registered in a body-scoped type space under [§21.10](#sec-local-type-declarations)'s restrictions (no visibility keyword or generic parameters, block-scoped, declared before use, absent from member signatures, no enclosing-generic-parameter reference, no reference to an enclosing body's local or parameter, no shadowing or same-body clash; a local `choice`/`class`/`interface` rejected).
- A nested type does not reference a type parameter of an enclosing type, which is not in scope in its declaration; it is one type whatever the enclosing type's instantiation ([§11.6](#sec-nested-types)).
- `owned` on an ordinary parameter distinguishes overloads exactly where [§22.6](#sec-overloading)'s declaration guard admits the pair (every differing position closed by language rule, for a pair of generic methods under each member's own constraints, against the [§28.1](#sec-where-the-owned-modifier-can-appear)-erasing and move-only substitutions); a pair failing the guard clashes at the second declaration ([§11.3](#sec-member-body)), and `owned` on an `out` parameter and `scoped` never distinguish ([§22.6](#sec-overloading)).
- Variant generic parameters (`in`, `out`) appear only in the appropriate position.
- A variant assignment whose source has a value-type type argument is rejected; the type itself (e.g. `IEnumerable<int>`) is fully usable, only the variant conversion is forbidden ([§12.9](#sec-variance)).
- Boxing a borrow-bearing record or a borrow-bearing inline array is subject to the same borrow-lifetime constraints as the unboxed value; the boxed value may not escape the source scope ([§8.6](#sec-boxing)). Move-only inline arrays (owning forms) cannot be boxed.
- An inline array's element type is never a move-only value type: `[N]C` or `[N]C?` over an owning choice `C` is a compile error, at the instantiation site for an element type that is a type parameter ([§15.1](#sec-inline-arrays), [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)).
- An inline array's element type is never an inline array (`[N][M]T`): a compile error, at the instantiation site for an element type that is a type parameter, and at the reference for a generic type alias whose expansion forms one ([§15.1](#sec-inline-arrays)).
- A write that lands in the [§8.6](#sec-boxing) box of a [§12.7](#sec-type-tests-is-is-not-as) value-narrowed carrier is a compile error in each of [§12.7](#sec-type-tests-is-is-not-as)'s three producing positions (the chain-extending store, the `ref`/`out` argument, the by-address `extern` inline-array argument) — the box is shared, so the write would be aliased mutation of a value — while assignment to the binding itself stores a fresh box and invalidates the narrowing.
- A concrete value-typed operand of `is`, `is not` or `as`, or a value-typed `case` scrutinee of [§19.3](#sec-patterns)'s kinds (a primitive, record, enum, choice, inline array, or the unit type) — by declared type, or its nullable form — is a compile error against a class, an interface (including one the value type implements), `string` or `Object` target or type pattern: the test could not discriminate at runtime and would need an implicit box, which neither position performs ([§8.6](#sec-boxing)); box explicitly. Where a type parameter stands on either side — operand or scrutinee, target or pattern — and at an instantiation a value meets a reference type, this rejection is not re-applied: the test is decided per instantiation, a bare test taking the answer the boxed value would give and a never-matching arm being admitted, while `as` and a type pattern with binding are rejected at the instantiation site, since a true answer would be the implicit box ([§12.7](#sec-type-tests-is-is-not-as), [§19.3](#sec-patterns)). The same concrete operand or scrutinee against a value type other than its own or its own nullable form, not a type parameter, is a compile error: the test could never succeed ([§12.7](#sec-type-tests-is-is-not-as), [§8.2](#sec-gettype)). Where a type parameter stands on either side and both sides are value types at an instantiation, the test is instead decided per instantiation — true for identical types (a nullable substitution of the target or pattern counting as its underlying type), false otherwise, a never-matching arm admitted — and is never rejected for its answer ([§12.7](#sec-type-tests-is-is-not-as), [§19.3](#sec-patterns)).
- `default(T)` is rejected for non-nullable reference types, for records whose declared fields include non-nullable references, and for inline arrays whose element type is a non-nullable reference type (including `[N owned]T` non-nullable owning forms) — non-defaultable types ([§17.11](#sec-the-default-operator); the `default(C)` row above carries the choice case).
- In an enum's value initializers, a reference to the constant being declared, or to a constant of the same enum declared after it, is a compile error; an earlier constant denotes its underlying value ([§10.2](#sec-explicit-values)).
- `default(T)` on an enum type with no declared zero-value constant is a compile error, as are `new T()` at such a substitution and default initialization of enum-typed storage — such an enum is not defaultable ([§17.11](#sec-the-default-operator)).
- `default(T)` is a compile error for a **constructor-only** record ([§9.9](#sec-constructor-only-records)) — a record declaring a constructor carrying a contract clause — as are `new T()` at such a substitution, default initialization of `R`-typed storage, and a `default(R)` default-value expression; such a record is not defaultable and does not satisfy `where T: new()` ([§17.11](#sec-the-default-operator), [§14.2](#sec-constraints)).
- A `with` expression requires a **record-typed** source: a class-typed source is a compile error at the `with` expression — the retired object-initializer form ([§9.5](#sec-non-destructive-update-with), [§22.11 *Object initializer blocks*](#sec-object-initializer-blocks)).
- A `with` expression whose source expression's static type is a constructor-only record is a compile error at the `with` expression ([§9.5](#sec-non-destructive-update-with), [§9.9](#sec-constructor-only-records)).
- An integer-to-enum cast `E(n)` is checked against the declared constants ([§5.4](#sec-enum-casts)): a constant operand equal to no declared constant is a compile error at the cast site; a non-constant operand equal to no declared constant raises `OverflowException` at runtime. No value of an enum type exists that is not equal to a declared constant.
- A shift count outside `0..width−1` of the left operand's type ([§6.5](#sec-bitwise-operations)) is a compile error when the count is a constant — including in constant-expression evaluation ([§17.14](#sec-constant-expressions)) — and raises `OverflowException` at runtime otherwise; `<<=`/`>>=` inherit the rule ([§6.6](#sec-compound-assignments)).
- An explicit conversion whose operand is a compile-time constant the conversion would reject is a compile error at the conversion site, never a deferred `OverflowException` ([§5.2](#sec-explicit-conversions), [§5.3](#sec-nullable-casts), and the enum-to-integer cast `I(e)` of [§5.4](#sec-enum-casts), which applies §5.2's conversion as its second step); a non-constant operand raises at runtime, and a saturating conversion is unaffected. The conversion expression is still not a constant expression ([§17.14](#sec-constant-expressions)).
- A collection literal targeting a reference type produces an owned value that must reach an owned location ([§15.4](#sec-collection-literals), [§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows)); one targeting an inline-array type produces a value, ownership arising only at `[N owned]…` slots ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)).
- Nullable field, property, or `ref`-parameter access — other than the narrowing `readonly`-field form — without copying to a local is rejected; only [§7.4](#sec-narrowing-applies-to-locals-only)'s narrowing carriers are narrowed, and a `ref` parameter never is, to non-null or to a type ([§7.4](#sec-narrowing-applies-to-locals-only), [§12.7](#sec-type-tests-is-is-not-as)).
- An `end`-label that is supplied — an identifier for named constructs, or a construct keyword (with operator token where applicable) for keyword-labelled constructs — must match the construct it closes; a mismatch is a compile error. The unlabelled form `end;` is always valid ([§1.6](#sec-statements-and-termination)).
- A `closed` class may be subclassed only within its declaring module; external subclasses are rejected. The spelling `sealed abstract` is rejected, the diagnostic naming `closed` ([§11.7](#sec-static-classes)).
- An enum implementing an interface must provide matching public members for every interface member; an interface declaring a settable property or indexer member is unconformable by any value kind — enums included ([§9.4](#sec-value-receivers-are-borrows), [§9.6](#sec-records-and-inheritance)).
- Calling `.Equals(Object?)`, `.Equals(T)`, or `.GetHashCode()` directly on a non-auto-hashable body record is a compile error at the call site with [§9.2](#sec-body-records)'s remedies (custom equality, `equality skip`, an auto-hashable shape); the error is **per member** and does not fire for a member the record declares itself ([§9.2](#sec-body-records)); a boxed receiver, `Object`- or interface-typed, reaches the record's declared `Equals(Object?)`/`GetHashCode` and otherwise the inherited identity members at runtime, a choice's box likewise per member ([§35.7](#sec-choice-equality)); a `T`-typed operand's use is read by its kind at the substitution, and a substitution with no member for that kind rejects the instantiation ([§9.2](#sec-equality-through-a-type-parameter)) — for a user-declared generic type's parameter, the constructed type at every site naming it, whether or not the member making the use is reached ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2), and a user declaration that names that type, or calls a generic method making such a use, at its own type parameter carries the requirement to its own instantiations ([§14.1](#sec-generic-declarations)); a standard-library equality search (`Contains`, `Remove`, `IndexOf`, `LastIndexOf`, `LinkedList<T>.Find`, the span family's `IndexOf`/`Contains`/`SequenceEqual`) at an element type with no member for the first kind is rejected at the call, the collection type itself staying well-formed, and in a generic body such a call at an element type involving a type parameter is that body's own `Equals` use ([§14.2](#sec-conditionally-admitted-members)'s register and rule 2).
- `=`, `<>`, `Equals` and `GetHashCode` on an inline array whose element type, nullability stripped, is not hashable, and `Contains` on one whose element type, nullability stripped, has no member for [§9.2](#sec-equality-through-a-type-parameter)'s first kind, are a compile error at the use site, and an inline array over a non-hashable element type, like a nullable `T?` over a non-hashable `T`, is not hashable ([§15.1.2](#sec-inline-array-members), [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties)).
- A storage component marked `equality skip` ([§9.2](#sec-equality-skip)) is removed from the auto-equality membership computation — every other role untouched, the generated `=` and `GetHashCode` computing over the same reduced set — under §9.2's placement discipline (storage components only; a non-storage member draws the inert-annotation compile error).

<a id="sec-appendix-c-visibility"></a>
### C.2 Visibility

- Every class member declares its visibility explicitly, except the member kinds user code can never invoke or name at a use site — currently `static constructor`, `destructor`, the `polymorphic` registry, and `invariant` members — which carry no visibility keyword ([§13.3](#sec-class-members)'s principle; [§22.16](#sec-class-invariants)).
- Every type appearing in a member's signature — field type, parameter type, return type, property type, indexer parameter and result type, types named in `where` constraints — is at least as visible as the member. The rule applies at every visibility level except `private`, which is unconstrained.
- A class's base class and implemented interfaces are at least as visible as the class.
- Top-level types are `public` or `internal` only.
- An explicit accessor visibility is no less restrictive than the property's overall visibility.
- An override declares the same visibility as the base member.

<a id="sec-appendix-c-resource-management"></a>
### C.3 Resource management

- An owning-classified choice ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)) is a move-only value type: disposal disposes the active case's `owned` payloads exactly once, on every path — scope end, exception edges, drop-on-overwrite (which disposes the displaced value automatically), discard, or a consuming match ([§35.5](#sec-owning-match)) ([K3](#sec-kernel-k3), [K5](#sec-kernel-k5)).
- An owning-classified choice cannot be boxed, is not directly sendable, and does not implement `IDisposable`; its disposal is discharged by its holder ([§35.8](#sec-choice-boxing), [§35.12](#sec-choice-sendability)).
- A choice that **holds borrows** ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)'s property, whatever the choice's classification) is subject to [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal)'s borrow-lifetime rules in full — the null-source forms, the escape bullets, the `async` position bans, and the live-local freeze contribution ([K2](#sec-kernel-k2) + [K5.5](#sec-kernel-k5)).

- `Dispose()` is generated for every non-static class ([K4.1](#sec-kernel-k4)'s backstop machinery).
- The compiler-generated `Dispose()` is thread-safe with respect to idempotency: concurrent calls execute disposal exactly once ([§28.2](#sec-the-idisposable-contract); K4.1).
- A class or record declaring a member named `Dispose`, at any parameter list, is a compile error at the declaration; the customization points are the `destructor` and `owned` fields ([§28.2](#sec-the-idisposable-contract), [§9.3](#sec-combined-form)'s collision posture). Interfaces are unaffected: the rule reaches classes and records only, and an interface may declare `Dispose()` itself.
- On construction unwind the throwing class's own `destructor` body is never run — every unwind edge disposes only the already-completed owned fields and, where completed, the base subobject — with [§22.9](#sec-owned-fields-and-exception-safety)'s one chaining-body exception and its [§7.9](#sec-definite-assignment-for-non-nullable-fields) ground ([#3245](https://github.com/s8lap/bezel-lang/issues/3245)).
- Owned fields are restricted to class- or interface-typed fields ([§28.5](#sec-owned-fields); not `string`, not function types, not value types; [K1.6](#sec-kernel-k1) + [K1.7](#sec-kernel-k1)).
- Assignment to an owned field or plain-`var` owned local disposes the displaced live value before storing — drop-on-overwrite, RHS-first ([§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields); [K3.11](#sec-kernel-k3)) — an owning-inline-array local or instance field taking the same rule per slot at whole-value reassignment ([§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)) and a static owning-inline-array field staying a plain store under [§22.13](#sec-static-initialization-order)'s posture with the [§22.12](#sec-static-members) form-(iv) warning.
- Owned values may not escape: transferring an owned field out requires an `owned` return, a bare owned-field read returns only as a receiver-sourced borrow (mint-announcing fields excepted — the [announcement table](#sec-announcement-table)'s rows 2–3), and a freshly-produced or `move`d owned value may not be assigned to a non-owned field ([§28.6](#sec-leak-prevention); [K9.1](#sec-kernel-k9) + K1.7 + [K2.3](#sec-kernel-k2)).
- A `new` expression's result, and any owned local, is disposed exactly once on every path — discharged by the program or auto-dropped at scope end with the must-use warning, suppressed by `using var`, explicit disposal, discard, move, or return ([§28.3](#sec-owned-local-discharge-requirement); [K3.14](#sec-kernel-k3)/[K3.15](#sec-kernel-k3)) — trivial-dispose values freed by the compiler with no demand on the program (K1.6, [§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types)), implicit boxing outside the rule ([§28.8](#sec-ownership-transfer)).
- A `static` method or operator whose declared return type (nullability stripped) is a class or interface type must announce its classification in the signature — the [announcement table](#sec-announcement-table)'s static column: `owned`, a mint-announcing type, or a bare type parameter with a non-empty potential source set — any other such signature (an empty-set bare-type-parameter return and a static-storage-returning method included) being a compile error at the declaration ([§28.3](#sec-factory-methods-and-sourceless-returns), [§28.3](#sec-bare-type-parameter-returns); [K2.4](#sec-kernel-k2)).
- An owning-collection or owning-wrapper return type declared without `owned` produces a **borrow** under the general borrow-return rules — the `Owning*` name denotes element ownership, orthogonal to the `owned` container qualifier, and the types are concrete, outside the mint-announcing families ([§28.3](#sec-borrow-lifetime-rules), [§28.6](#sec-leak-prevention); [K1.5](#sec-kernel-k1) + [K2.4](#sec-kernel-k2)).
- A call whose declared (pre-substitution, nullability-stripped) return type is **mint-announcing** produces an owned frame at every callee kind, and callee-side the unmarked mint-announcing return is container-ownership-transferring with stored-borrow returns rejected, the [§29.1](#sec-iterator-protocol) self-returning enumerator's `return this;` being the one admitted receiver return — the [announcement table](#sec-announcement-table)'s rows 2–3 (*Calls mint for the mint-announcing families*, [§28.3](#sec-producers); [K6.2](#sec-kernel-k6)/[K6.3](#sec-kernel-k6), with axiom [A15](#sec-axiom-register)'s one admission).
- A member carrying, anywhere within a parameter's declared type, a function type whose return slot (nullability stripped) is a bare type parameter is inadmissible at an instantiation substituting a `Task`-family type for that parameter ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rules 2/4), while the iterable family carries no per-substitution exclusion — its laundering inhabitants are rejected inhabitant-side ([§28.3](#sec-bare-type-parameter-returns), [§27.1.1](#sec-function-type-assignability), [§27.6](#sec-method-references)).
- A member is inadmissible at an instantiation substituting a function type for a type parameter that occurs, within a parameter's declared type, inside a parameter slot of a function type occupying a parameter slot of that type ([§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rules 2/4; [§28.3](#sec-bare-type-parameter-returns); K1.6 + K2.4).
- Explicit `Dispose()` requires an **owned receiver** and is a compile error through a borrow, with no exception — element borrows from borrowing-family collections included, the retired carve recorded at the axiom register's A8 tombstone — while every other operation on a borrowed owning collection remains available ([§28.6](#sec-who-may-dispose), [§28.6](#sec-borrowed-owning-collections); [K3.9](#sec-kernel-k3), its [consume-table](#sec-consume-table) row).
- An unbound owned temporary is disposed exactly once — at the end of its full expression after its uses complete, or during unwinding in reverse production order ([§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries); K1 + K3.15 + [K8.1](#sec-kernel-k8)).
- A binding-atom binding whose initializer is an owned production ([§17.15](#sec-the-binding-atom)) is a named unbound owned temporary bounded by the atom — disposed exactly once at the atom boundary unless a [K3](#sec-kernel-k3) position discharged it, no borrow or frame sourced by it escaping the atom ([§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries); [K8.4](#sec-kernel-k8)/[K8.5](#sec-kernel-k8)).
- An `out owned` parameter is a callee-local owned slot until normal return — disposed by the callee's exception-path discharge on a later throw, transferring to the caller's recipient exactly on normal return, the caller-side obligation attaching on normal-completion paths only ([§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers), [§22.4](#sec-inline-out-declarations); K3 + K3.15).
- An inline `out var x` recipient adopts the resolved parameter's announced classification (a borrow against `out`, an owned local against `out owned`); `out using var x` is admitted only against an `out owned` parameter; a pre-declared **local** is admitted as an `out owned` recipient only in an adoptable state, adopts owned once, and is state-matched from the call's normal return; no field, indexer slot, or property target is admitted at `out owned` ([§22.3](#sec-ref-and-out-argument-locations), [§22.4](#sec-inline-out-declarations), [§22.6](#sec-overloading); K1.7 + K3.11).
- A `ref` or `out` argument names no location of move-only value type, a location whose declared type is or contains a type parameter included at each instantiation that makes it one ([§22.3](#sec-ref-and-out-argument-locations), [§3.6](#sec-derived-type-properties) rule 2); a `ref` parameter, a function type's `ref` slot included, is not declared at a move-only value type ([§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers), [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types)).
- `using var` variables may not be reassigned (axiom [A5](#sec-axiom-register)).
- A `using var` or `await using var` whose initializer is an unmarked read (`x` or `x!`, parenthesized or not) of a named owned binding whose declared type, nullability stripped, is a class or interface type — a bare type parameter included — is rejected; `move x` adopts (not over a `using var` source, axiom [A5](#sec-axiom-register)) and a `var` or `const` binding views (the anonymous form: delete it) ([§28.10](#sec-using-var); [K3.4](#sec-kernel-k3)).
- Records may not have `owned` fields, may not have inline-array fields with the `owned` slot marker, may not have destructors, may not implement `IDisposable` (K1.7 — copy-semantics holders cannot hold obligations).
- At a control-flow merge point, a variable that was owned on one branch and borrowed on the other is rejected ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows); [K7.3](#sec-kernel-k7)). The two branches must be equalized before the merge.
- A local holding no classified value — **uninitialized**, or in the **polymorphic-null** state — adopts the ownership classification of the first assignment reaching it on each path, and is state-matched thereafter; a join at which one edge leaves it uninitialized leaves it not definitely assigned, each assigning edge's obligation carried per-path ([§28.3](#sec-ownership-state-of-locals); K1.7 + K3.11, [K3.14](#sec-kernel-k3)).
- A method reference that captures a borrowed receiver is subject to the same closure-escape rules as a lambda capturing a borrow ([§28.3](#sec-local-variables-ownership-and-borrows), [§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types); K2.3).
- A function value with a non-empty source set is not stored into a function-typed holder: a property or indexer assignment, whatever the accessor form; an argument for a function-typed record component at the record's generated constructor, or a `with` assignment to one; a function-typed choice payload at a case construction; or a slot of an inline array whose declared element type is a function type, a local array's included ([§28.3](#sec-borrow-lifetime-rules) *function-typed holders*; K2.4).
- No function value with a non-empty source set reaches a set-erasing position: a position declared `Object`, or a parameter, return slot, `ref` or `out` location, record component, choice payload or inline-array slot declared at a bare type parameter that the instantiation substitutes with a function type, nor the result of invoking an argument bound to a function-typed parameter whose return slot is such a type parameter ([§28.3](#sec-borrow-lifetime-rules)'s closure bullet; K2.3 + K2.4).
- A method reference is not formed with a function-typed parameter slot bound to a set-erasing callee parameter ([§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters) *method-reference formation bar*; K2.4).
- `scoped` is declared only on a function-typed parameter or field, or on a class- or interface-typed parameter whose declared type, nullability stripped, is not `Object` ([§22.3](#sec-parameter-modifiers), [§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters)).
- A value-typed argument at an interface-typed `scoped` parameter is admitted only where [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal) admits storing it in an instance field of a class (not borrow-bearing, or in the null-source form); it has no borrow source and freezes nothing ([§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters), [§8.6](#sec-boxing)).
- A closure that captures a `ref` or `out` parameter, whatever the parameter's type, carries the declaring body's scope in its source set and so does not outlive the call, nor does a deferred-activation frame that carries it, a task-returning call that would carry it in a synchronous body being rejected; an assignment through it does not discharge an `out` parameter's must-assign obligation ([§27.5](#sec-closures), [§28.3](#sec-borrow-lifetime-rules); K2.3 + K2.4).
- A call-bounded function-typed parameter is not stored into any collection, a local one included; a frame carrying it may be held in a purely local collection ([§28.14](#sec-scoped-callback-parameters); K2.4).
- An assignment of a borrow-carrying value to an instance property of a class or interface, other than through `set(owned)`, is admitted only where the same store into a non-`owned` field of the receiver would be, and one to a static property only where the same store into a non-`owned` static field of its declared type (`readonly` for a `static readonly` auto-property) would be, whatever the accessor form ([§28.3](#sec-borrow-lifetime-rules) *property stores of a borrow-carrying value*; K2.3).
- A borrow-bearing record, a borrow-bearing inline array, or a choice that holds borrows ([§35.4](#sec-choice-classification)'s holds-borrows property) may be stored in a static field only when every reference-typed field or payload (and every reference-typed slot of every inline-array field) of the value, through nested record and choice components, is null (the null-source form, [§9.7](#sec-records-and-disposal); K2.3 — the always-live holder admits only **reference-free** values: every reference-typed field or payload null, not merely every borrow-carrying one).
- A trivial-dispose class has its discharge performed by the compiler — no warning, no user code, logical disposal plus reclamation at the statically-known owner's release point ([§28.9](#sec-runtime-managed-types), [§28.2](#sec-checked-disposal); K1.6).
- An owning inline array's live slots are disposed in **reverse slot order** at every ending — scope end, the containing class's destructor, and whole-value reassignment — under [§28.4](#sec-the-destructor)'s multi-value-cleanup discipline ([§15.1.1](#sec-owning-inline-arrays), [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types), [§28.7](#sec-reassigning-owned-fields)). A **wholly** moved-from move-only local carries no restoration obligation; a moved-from slot, and a whole-value `move` out of a field, do ([K9.2](#sec-kernel-k9)).
- A `_ := expression;` discard statement disposes any owned class, interface, or move-only value at end of statement, by runtime type — rejected only for the `Task` family (`Task`, `Task<T>`, `OwningTask<T>`), whose routed spelling is `Task.FireAndForget` ([§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_); K3.9 + [K4.2](#sec-kernel-k4), axiom [A6](#sec-axiom-register)).
- A class implementing `IAsyncDisposable` without a destructor receives a compiler warning ([§28.12](#sec-asynchronous-disposal)).
- The `move x.f` expression is permitted only on an owned instance field, leaves the field moved-from, and obligates every control-flow path from the move to the method's exit — exception edges included — to reassign the slot ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression); [K9.1](#sec-kernel-k9)/[K9.2](#sec-kernel-k9)).
- The `move coll[i]` expression ([§28.8.1](#sec-the-move-expression), [§28.11](#sec-collections-do-not-own-elements)) is permitted only on the receivers §28.11 lists, each of whose indexer names an owned slot (no interface-typed receiver, `IOwningList<T>` included); the slot is left in moved-from state (K9.1). The same field-restoration rule applies (K9.2, per-slot), with constant indices tracked per-slot and non-constant indices tracked conservatively at the whole-collection level.
- Owned-element collections own their elements — owned-ingress members take owned arguments, the indexer-set and the removing members dispose, `Dispose` cascades, default iteration borrows, and ownership leaves only through `Drain` and the `Pop*` members ([§28.11](#sec-collections-do-not-own-elements); K1 per slot, axiom [A9](#sec-axiom-register)).
- Iterator yield ownership is determined by the iterator's declared return type — enumerator-owned yields with a borrowing iteration variable at the non-owning heads, per-`MoveNext` transfer to an owned iteration variable at the `IOwning*` heads ([§29.2](#sec-iterator-yield-ownership); [K6.2](#sec-kernel-k6)).
- In an owning iterator, `yield return x;` on a named owned binding is a marker-free consume joining the consume-site freeze (the [consume table](#sec-consume-table)'s [K3.7](#sec-kernel-k3) row; [K5.1](#sec-kernel-k5)); in a borrowing iterator the same unmarked read is a re-borrow of the frame-resident binding ([§29.2](#sec-desugaring-of-for), [§28.3](#sec-move-semantics-for-owned-locals)).
- A discard statement `_ := x;` over a named owned binding is a marker-free consume and a site-announced kill — disposed at end of statement, the binding left explicitly-disposed, no freeze, no transfer marker ([§17.13](#sec-the-discard-_), [§28.3](#sec-move-semantics-for-owned-locals); K4.2 + [K5.3](#sec-kernel-k5)).
- A closure may read a captured owned binding (as a borrow) but may not assign to it, transfer from it, or dispose it ([§28.3](#sec-captured-owned-bindings); K2 + [K5.5](#sec-kernel-k5)).
- The must-use warning covers undischarged `owned` parameters of iterators and async methods, attached at the parameter declaration, at every non-trivial-dispose declared type ([§28.3](#sec-owned-local-discharge-requirement), [§28.9](#sec-trivial-dispose-classes), [§29.8](#sec-iterators-with-owned-parameters), [§30.1](#sec-async-methods); K3.14 + [K1.6](#sec-kernel-k1)).
- A returned deferred-activation frame may carry only parameter- or receiver-sourced borrows — its carried sources being what its building calls' receivers and plain arguments contribute ([§28.3](#sec-argument-contributions)), a plain function-typed argument's capture-set contribution ([§28.3](#sec-unbound-owned-temporaries)) and, in a generic body, a type-parameter-typed argument's contribution at every substitution its constraints admit among them; carrying a scope-bound local's, `using var`'s, or temporary's borrow out through the return, directly or through a callback's capture, is rejected ([§28.3](#sec-returning-a-deferred-activation-frame); K6.2 + K2.4).
- A fresh-producer element of non-trivial-dispose class type in a borrowing-family collection literal is rejected (bind the source first, or use the owning family), a trivial-dispose fresh element instead joining the literal tree as an aggregate-owned node, and `Add`/`Insert`/indexer-set keeping their admissions with the [§15.4](#sec-collection-literals) store warning on fresh unbound owned temporaries ([§15.4](#sec-collection-literals), [§28.11](#sec-borrowing-collections); [K8.4](#sec-kernel-k8) + K2.3).
- A stdlib §5 class-element terminal accessor or no-selector aggregation call whose receiver's statically-traced provenance roots at a directly-called same-unit iterator with at least one reachable **enumerator-owned** yield — minted or adopted, [§29.2](#sec-iterator-yield-ownership)'s two arms — draws the terminal-accessor provenance warning, acceptance unchanged; at a class or interface element type a materializer result and a `GroupBy` grouping are pass-through nodes of that trace, never roots. The member set, the predicate, the pass-through nodes, and the exhaustive silent-root set are normative at [§29.11](#sec-multiple-enumeration) (predicate widened).
- A call to a [§29.12](#sec-mutation-during-iteration) structural operation whose receiver is the same binding the enclosing `for`/`await for` iterates, in the loop's own callable body, from which the loop's next advance is reachable, draws the mutation-during-iteration warning, acceptance unchanged; a call followed on every path by an exit from the loop is exempt, a call inside a nested lambda or local type body the loop does not sequence is outside the rule, and a modification through a different binding is not traced ([§29.12](#sec-mutation-during-iteration)).
- A use of an owning-collection element borrow — an indexer-get, a default-iteration variable, or a §29.11-traced class-element accessor result rooted at the collection — after a dominating `Clear()`, `Remove` of the borrow, or `RemoveAt` at the borrow's index with no intervening structural operation on the binding, on the same collection binding, draws the element-borrow use-after-removal warning, acceptance unchanged; an indexer-set and a keyed dictionary removal are not in the kill set and a re-taken borrow is clean ([§28.11](#sec-owning-collections); [K4.2](#sec-kernel-k4) + [K7.4](#sec-kernel-k7)).
- Implicit discharge — auto-drop, exception-path cleanup, drop-on-overwrite, cascades, frame teardown — always takes the synchronous `Dispose()` path; only `await using` (or an awaited direct `DisposeAsync()`) runs asynchronous cleanup ([§28.12](#sec-asynchronous-disposal); the implicit forms are K3.14/K3.15, K3.11, [K9](#sec-kernel-k9)'s cascade, and [K6](#sec-kernel-k6)'s frame teardown).

<a id="sec-appendix-c-generics"></a>
### C.4 Generics

- `where T: sendable` substitutions are types whose sendable derived type property ([§30.14](#sec-sendable-types)) holds; checked per instantiation after substitution ([§14.2](#sec-constraints)).

- `where T: notnull` substitutions are non-nullable types; a nullable type, value or reference, does not satisfy the constraint.
- `where T: class` substitutions are non-nullable reference types: classes (including `Array<T>`, `OwningArray<T>`), interfaces, `string`, function types.
- `where T: value` substitutions are non-nullable value types: records, enums, choices ([§35](#sec-choices)), primitives, inline arrays (all forms, including owning `[N owned]…` forms — see [§15.3](#sec-move-only-value-types) for restrictions on copy operations in the generic body), the unit type. A nullable value type (e.g. `int?`) does not satisfy the constraint ([§14.2](#sec-constraints)).
- `where T: SomeClass` substitutions are non-nullable subtypes of `SomeClass` — class types only (no interfaces, since interfaces do not extend classes).
- `where T: IFoo` substitutions are non-nullable types conforming to `IFoo` per the [§14.2](#sec-constraints) conformance rule: classes implementing it (directly, by inheritance, or implicitly — `IDisposable`), records and enums implementing it directly, interfaces extending it (directly or transitively), primitives conforming through their stdlib declarations or the compiler-provided conformances ([§14.2](#sec-constraints) clause 5, [§11.8](#sec-static-interface-members)), and type parameters whose constraints guarantee it.
- `where T: new()` substitutions are class types with a `public` parameterless constructor — `abstract` and `closed` classes excluded ([§12.5](#sec-abstract-classes-and-members)) — or defaultable value types ([§17.11](#sec-the-default-operator)), every nullable value type among them; `new T()` for a value substitution is `default(T)`, `null` at a nullable one; a nullable reference type satisfies neither arm ([§14.2](#sec-constraints)).
- Constraint combinations are checked for consistency (`class, value` is rejected).
- A declared constraint whose satisfaction turns on a type parameter in scope — the argument is or contains one, or, under `where T: U`, the bound's argument does — is decided at the naming, holding where it holds at every substitution those parameters' constraints admit; a parameter has a derived property there only by carrying the same constraint ([§14.2](#sec-constraints)).
- Inside an unconstrained generic body, `T` is treated conservatively as possibly nullable.
- `?` is idempotent under substitution: `T?` with T = `U?` denotes `U?` (no two-level optional; [§7.10](#sec-generics-and-nullability)).
- Type-bound constraints (`where T: class`, `where T: SomeClass`, `where T: IFoo`) and `where T: notnull` make T non-nullable inside the body.
- `owned` is not admitted on generic type arguments ([§14.4](#sec-owned-as-a-generic-argument)). The owning collection and task types are separate named classes (`OwningArray<T>`, `OwningTask<T>`, etc., declared in stdlib [§4](Bezel_Standard_Library.md#sec-system-collections-generic) and [§6](Bezel_Standard_Library.md#sec-system-threading)); each carries `where T: class` (or `where V: class` for `OwningDictionary<K, V>`) as part of its declaration.
- An `override` of a generic method and a method implementing a generic interface method inherit the overridden or implemented declaration's constraints: a restated `where` clause states an equivalent set and a differing one is a compile error; a base-class method satisfies an interface method only with an equivalent constraint set; a method implementing or overriding declarations whose sets are not equivalent is a compile error ([§14.2](#sec-constraints-on-overrides)).
- Type-argument inference for generic methods follows [§14.5](#sec-type-argument-inference); constraints are checked after inference, on the completed substitution, and are not inference sources.
- A generic extension's head binds each bare identifier at one argument position only; an identifier repeated across positions (`extension Dictionary<K, K>`) is rejected ([§26.4](#sec-generic-extensions)).
- A generic extension's head is checked against the extended type's declared constraints under the block's own `where` clause; the block's parameters inherit no constraint from the extended type (`extension OwningArray<T> where T: class`) ([§26.4](#sec-generic-extensions)).

<a id="sec-methods-constructors-and-accessors"></a>
### C.5 Methods, constructors, and accessors

- Modifier order matches [§11.5](#sec-modifier-order).
- A constructor's `base(...)` or `this(...)` call appears in the chain position before the body, not as a statement in the body (see [§12.8](#sec-constructor-chaining) and grammar A.4 `CtorChain`).
- Field initializers run exactly once per instance construction — as step 2 of the constructor whose chain position holds `base(...)` or the implicit `base()`; a `this(...)`-chaining constructor skips them ([§22.8](#sec-field-initializers)).
- A class with a primary constructor permits `base(...)` only on the primary constructor; non-primary constructors must chain with `this(...)`.
- A `this(...)` chain is acyclic: no constructor reaches itself by following the `this(...)` calls of its type's constructors ([§12.8](#sec-constructor-chaining)).
